parts_head.eyebrow: Try It in the Model · 在模型裡試試

parts.text_en: The three strokes of 川 stand side by side, so they are written from the left: the left-falling stroke, the short vertical in the middle, and the long vertical on the right.
parts.text_zh: 「川」三筆左右並排，從左邊寫起：左邊的撇、中間的短豎、右邊的長豎。

parts.text_en: The three horizontal strokes of 三 are stacked, so they go from the top down. Look at the lengths, too: the middle one is the shortest, and the bottom one is the longest.
parts.text_zh: 「三」三橫上下疊在一起，從上往下寫。也看看長短：中間最短、最下面最長。

parts.meta_zh: 教育部例字：十、干、士、甘、聿
parts.text_en: In 十 the horizontal and vertical strokes cross, so the horizontal comes first.
parts.text_zh: 「十」橫豎相交，所以先寫橫，再寫豎。

parts.text_en: In 人 the right-falling stroke starts on the left-falling one, so the left-falling stroke comes first.
parts.text_zh: 「人」的捺從撇的中間出發，兩筆相接，所以先撇後捺。

parts.text_en: In 小 the vertical hook stands in the middle and does not cross the two dots, so it comes first; then the left dot, then the right dot.
parts.text_zh: 「小」中間的豎鉤不和兩點相交，所以先寫；再寫左點、右點。

parts.text_en: 日 is a box. First the left side, then the top and the right side in one turning stroke, then the stroke inside, and the bottom line last to close the box. Closing it last leaves room to place the inside stroke well.
parts.text_zh: 「日」是四面圍起來的結構：先寫左邊的豎，再一筆寫上面和右邊（橫折鉤），接著寫裡面的橫，最後才用底下的橫封口。最後才封口，裡面那一橫才放得好。

lessons.parts_note_en: Each card's example comes from the Ministry of Education's list. Tap Watch it in 3D, then try Backward in the model.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 每張卡片的例字都取自教育部的列表。點「在模型中看」，再在模型裡試試「倒過來寫」。

guess.lead_en: All the strokes are shown in gray. Tap them one by one in the standard order. A right answer turns black and gets a number; a wrong one flashes red, with a hint about the rule.
guess.lead_zh: 字的每一筆都先畫成灰色，照標準筆順一筆一筆點。點對了那一筆變黑、標上數字；點錯了會閃紅色，並提示這個字用的法則。

ri.en: Outside, then inside, then close the bottom!
ri.zh: 先外圍、再裡面、最後封口！

pad.lead_en: Choose a character and trace it in the order of the blue numbers. After each stroke, the chart compares your press-and-lift curve with the brush's for that stroke.
pad.lead_zh: 選一個字，照藍色數字的順序描寫。每寫完一筆，圖上就把你的提按曲線和毛筆那一筆比較。

tips.en: Say the rule out loud before you start, for example “outside, inside, close.”
tips.zh: 下筆前先唸出法則，例如「先外、後內、再封口」。

tips.en: In 日, make the bottom line touch both sides but not stick out past the right side.
tips.zh: 寫「日」的封口橫要碰到兩邊，但不要超出右邊。

tips.en: In 三, keep the middle line short and the bottom line long.
tips.zh: 寫「三」時，中間短、下面長。

links_head.eyebrow: Before and Next · 上一課與下一課
links_head.en: From the eight principles to the story of writing

links.en: Can One Character Teach You Every Stroke?
links.zh: 永字八法：一個字學會所有筆畫？
links.note_en: The five strokes of 永 follow the same rules: the dot first, the box-like turn next, and the right-falling stroke last.
links.note_zh: 「永」的五畫也照這些法則：先點、再橫折鉤，最後才是捺。

links.k_zh: 下一課・第五課・單元二
links.en: Where Did Chinese Characters Come From?
links.zh: 漢字從哪裡來？甲骨文到篆書
links.note_en: Marks carved on tortoise shells and ox bones, writing cast in bronze, and the even lines of seal script: how characters looked before the brush shaped them.
links.note_zh: 刻在龜甲牛骨上的字、鑄在青銅器上的字、線條勻稱的篆書：在毛筆讓字變成今天的樣子以前，漢字長什麼樣。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories of Stroke Order · 筆順的故事
culture_cards.title_en: Seventeen rules, a tiny hook, a grid like 井, and the first page of an old copybook
culture_cards.title_zh: 十七條法則、一個小鉤、井字格，和舊習字簿的第一頁
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how people learn to write in order.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於「照順序寫字」的四個小故事。

cards.zh: 十七條法則與一個網站
cards.body_en: Taiwan's Ministry of Education sums up stroke order in 17 basic rules in its handbook of standard characters. Its stroke-order website opened for trial use in 2008 with the 4,808 common characters. In 2020 it grew to 6,057 characters and dropped the word “common” from its name, and in 2024 it reached 6,063 characters.
cards.body_zh: 教育部在《常用國字標準字體筆順手冊》裡，把筆順歸納成 17 條基本法則。教育部的筆順學習網 2008 年試用，收錄 4,808 個常用字；2020 年擴充到 6,057 字，網站名稱也拿掉了「常用」兩個字；2024 年再擴充到 6,063 字。

cards.en: Why 日 has a hook and 口 does not
cards.body_en: The ministry's website answers this question. In 口 the second stroke turns without a hook and leans inward, ready to meet the closing stroke, because there is nothing inside. In 日 the second stroke ends with a small hook, because the brush is already turning toward the next stroke inside the box. The hook shows the flow of the brush.
cards.body_zh: 教育部的網站回答過這個問題：「口」裡面沒有其他筆畫，第二筆是「橫折」不帶鉤，折筆往內斜，準備接最後一筆封口；「日」框裡還有筆畫，第二筆是「橫折鉤」，鉤起來是因為毛筆已經準備寫框裡的下一筆，是筆勢使然。

cards.body_en: The ministry's dictionary describes the nine-square grid as practice paper for copying models: each large square is divided like the character 井 into nine smaller squares, so learners can match the model and place every dot and line. The 田 grid and the 米 grid do the same job.
cards.body_zh: 教育部辭典說，九宮格是臨帖用的界格紙：每一大格用「井」字形分成九小格，方便臨摹時對照範本字形、掌握點畫的部位。另有田字格、米字格，功用相當。

cards.en: 上大人, 孔乙己: the first page
cards.body_en: Long ago, children starting school traced red characters in a copybook that began 上大人，孔乙己，化三千，七十士. These characters were chosen because they have very few strokes. Tracing red models like this is called 描紅, the same idea as the faint red characters on this lesson's practice pad.
cards.body_zh: 從前學童入學時，用描紅的習字簿練字，上面寫著「上大人，孔乙己，化三千，七十士」，因為這些字筆畫簡少，方便學習。照著紅色範字一筆一筆描，就叫「描紅」，和這一課練字板上淡紅色的範字是同一個道理。

myths.myth_en: If the finished character looks right, stroke order does not matter.
myths.myth_zh: 字寫出來看起來對，筆順就不重要。
myths.fact_en: The result can look similar, but stroke order is a shared standard that teachers, textbooks, and the ministry's website all use. It also follows the flow of the brush, and later, when you write faster, strokes begin to join in the order you write them.
myths.fact_zh: 寫出來可能看起來差不多，但筆順是老師、課本和教育部網站共同使用的標準；它也順著毛筆的筆勢；以後寫得快的時候，筆畫會照書寫的順序連起來。

myths.myth_en: Stroke order is just one rule: top to bottom, left to right.
myths.myth_zh: 筆順只有一條規則：由上而下、由左而右。
myths.fact_en: The ministry lists 17 basic rules. Some go against “top to bottom” at first glance: in 小 the middle vertical comes first, and in 日 the bottom line comes last.
myths.fact_zh: 教育部列了 17 條基本法則。有的乍看不是「由上而下」：「小」要先寫中間的豎，「日」的底下那一橫最後寫。

myths.myth_en: The box of 日 is drawn as one stroke.
myths.myth_zh: 「日」外面的框是一筆畫完的。
myths.fact_en: The box takes three strokes: the left vertical, the top and right side in one turning stroke, and the bottom line, which is written last to close the box.
myths.fact_zh: 外框要三筆：左邊的豎、一筆寫上面和右邊的橫折鉤，還有最後才寫、用來封口的底下那一橫。

myths.myth_en: Stroke order only matters for brush calligraphy.
myths.myth_zh: 只有寫毛筆字才需要筆順。
myths.fact_en: The standard order belongs to the character, not to the tool, so it is the same for pencils and pens. In Taiwan's curriculum for grades 3 and 4, children write mainly with pencils and pens, with the brush as a supplement.
myths.fact_zh: 標準筆順跟著字走，不跟著筆走，鉛筆、原子筆也一樣。台灣國語文課綱第二學習階段（三、四年級）的寫字，以硬筆為主、毛筆為輔。

tricks.title_en: Left to right, top to bottom
tricks.body_en: Most characters start at the upper left.
tricks.body_zh: 大部分的字從左上開始寫。

tricks.body_en: When they cross, the horizontal goes first: 十.
tricks.body_zh: 橫豎相交先寫橫：十。

tricks.body_en: When they meet, the left-falling stroke goes first: 人.
tricks.body_zh: 撇捺相接先寫撇：人。

tricks.title_en: Go in, then close the door
tricks.body_en: Outside, then inside, then the bottom line: 日.
tricks.body_zh: 先外圍、再裡面、最後封口：日。

safety.en: Ink stains clothes and is very hard to wash out. Wear old clothes or an apron, and roll up your sleeves.
safety.zh: 墨沾到衣服很難洗掉：穿舊衣服或圍裙，袖子捲起來。

safety.en: Cover the desk with old newspaper, and keep the ink in a heavy, steady dish so it will not tip over.
safety.zh: 桌上先鋪舊報紙；墨要裝在重一點、放得穩的碟子裡，免得打翻。

safety.en: Press gently. Crushing the brush against the paper squashes the hairs and can split or break them.
safety.zh: 輕輕地按就好：把筆用力壓在紙上，筆毛會擠扁，也可能分岔或折斷。

safety.en: Do not put the brush, the ink, or the ink stick in your mouth, and do not lick the brush tip to shape it.
safety.zh: 毛筆、墨汁、墨條都不要放進嘴裡，也不要用嘴巴舔筆尖。

safety.en: After writing, wash the brush in clean water until the water runs clear, gently shape it into a point, and hang it tip-down or lay it flat to dry. Wash your hands, too.
safety.zh: 寫完後用清水洗筆，洗到水變清為止；輕輕把筆毛理成尖形，筆尖朝下掛起來或平放晾乾。也要洗手。

materials.en: Enough space for everyone to stretch out an arm
materials.zh: 每個人都能伸直手臂的空間

materials.en: The six example characters on the board: 川、三、十、人、小、日
materials.zh: 黑板上寫好六個例字：川、三、十、人、小、日

materials.en: Later: brushes, water, and old newspaper
materials.zh: 之後用：毛筆、清水、舊報紙

steps.en: Everyone stands and writes a character in the air with the whole arm, as big as possible, counting the strokes out loud: one, two, three.
steps.zh: 全班站起來，用整隻手臂在空中把字寫得越大越好，一邊大聲數筆順：一、二、三。

steps.en: The teacher watches for anyone moving in a different order and stops to ask which rule applies.
steps.zh: 老師看誰的順序不一樣，停下來問：這個字用的是哪一條法則？

steps.en: Repeat with your eyes closed. Can you still feel where each stroke starts?
steps.zh: 閉上眼睛再寫一次：還感覺得到每一筆從哪裡開始嗎？

steps.en: Finish by writing the same characters with water on newspaper, saying the numbers as you go.
steps.zh: 最後用清水在報紙上寫同樣的字，邊寫邊唸數字。

activities.tip_en: Big arm movements make the order easy for the teacher to see, and students remember movements better than lists.
activities.tip_zh: 手臂動作大，老師一眼就看得出順序；而且動作比條列的規則更容易記住。

materials.en: A large sheet of paper with a nine-square grid for each team, taped to the wall
materials.zh: 每組一大張畫好九宮格的紙，貼在牆上

materials.en: A thick marker or a brush with water for each team
materials.zh: 每組一枝粗的麥克筆，或一枝蘸清水的毛筆

materials.en: A tablet or computer with the Ministry of Education's stroke-order website
materials.zh: 一台能開教育部筆順學習網的平板或電腦

steps.en: The teacher names a character. The first student in each team runs up and writes only the first stroke.
steps.zh: 老師說一個字，每組第一位同學跑上前，只寫第一筆。

steps.en: The next student writes the second stroke, and so on, until the character is finished.
steps.zh: 下一位寫第二筆，依序接力，直到把字寫完。

steps.en: Check the order with the stroke-order animation on the ministry's website. Each correct stroke earns a point.
steps.zh: 用教育部筆順學習網的動畫核對順序，每一筆寫對得一分。

steps.en: Talk about the strokes that teams got wrong. Which rule would have helped?
steps.zh: 討論大家寫錯的那幾筆：哪一條法則能幫上忙？

activities.tip_en: Start with the six characters from this lesson, then try 田 and 山 from the ministry's examples.
activities.tip_zh: 先從這一課的六個例字開始，再試試教育部例字裡的「田」和「山」。

sources.en: The 17 basic rules of stroke order, with example characters for each, from the Handbook of Standard Characters
sources.zh: 依《常用國字標準字體筆順手冊》歸納的 17 條筆順基本法則與例字
sources.src: 教育部《國字標準字體筆順學習網》〈筆順基本原則〉

sources.en: English version of the rules (lists 人 as an example of left-falling before right-falling)
sources.zh: 法則的英文版（先撇後捺的例字列了「人」）
sources.src: Ministry of Education, “Basic Rules of Stroke Order”

sources.en: Website history: trial version 2008 (ROC year 97), 4,808 common characters; 2020 expanded to 6,057 and renamed; 2024 expanded to 6,063; the site design uses 上大人孔乙己 as practice characters for beginners
sources.zh: 網站版次：民國 97 年試用版、4,808 個常用字；109 年擴充為 6,057 字並更名；113 年 6,063 字；內頁以初學者練字例「上大人孔乙己」設計
sources.src: 教育部《國字標準字體筆順學習網》〈網站介紹〉

sources.en: Why the second stroke of 日 ends with a hook and that of 口 does not (the flow of the brush); practice mode checks each stroke
sources.zh: 「日」第二筆為什麼帶鉤、「口」不帶鉤（筆勢使然）；筆順練習會檢查每一筆
sources.src: 教育部《國字標準字體筆順學習網》〈常見問題集〉

sources.en: Stroke order: the order in which the strokes of a character are written
sources.zh: 筆順：書寫文字時，筆畫先後的順序
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「筆順」

sources.en: Nine-square grid: practice paper divided like 井 into nine squares; the 田 grid and 米 grid do the same job
sources.zh: 九宮格：臨帖所用的界格紙，「井」字形分九小格；另有田字格、米字格，功用相當
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「九宮格」

sources.en: 上大人: the old copybook children traced when starting school, “上大人，孔乙己，化三千，七十士”, chosen for its few strokes
sources.zh: 上大人：舊時學童入學時描紅的習字簿，筆畫簡少，便利學童學習
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「上大人」

sources.en: 描紅: tracing red model characters printed on practice paper, stroke by stroke
sources.zh: 描紅：用紅色將字套印在習字紙上，按照紅字範本一點一畫依樣描寫
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「描紅」

sources.en: Taiwan's curriculum, learning stage 2 (grades 3 and 4), 4-II-7: writing mainly with pencils and pens, with the brush as a supplement
sources.zh: 十二年國教國語文第二學習階段 4-Ⅱ-7：習寫以硬筆字為主，毛筆為輔
sources.src: 國家教育研究院《語文領域－國語文課程手冊》（2018）

sources.en: Stroke order of 川 (3 strokes)
sources.zh: 「川」3 畫的筆順
sources.src: 教育部《國字標準字體筆順學習網》「川」

sources.en: Stroke order of 三 (3 strokes)
sources.zh: 「三」3 畫的筆順
sources.src: 教育部《國字標準字體筆順學習網》「三」

sources.en: Stroke order of 十 (2 strokes)
sources.zh: 「十」2 畫的筆順
sources.src: 教育部《國字標準字體筆順學習網》「十」

sources.en: Stroke order of 人 (2 strokes)
sources.zh: 「人」2 畫的筆順
sources.src: 教育部《國字標準字體筆順學習網》「人」

sources.en: Stroke order of 小 (3 strokes): the vertical hook, then the left dot, then the right dot
sources.zh: 「小」3 畫：豎鉤、左點、右點
sources.src: 教育部《國字標準字體筆順學習網》「小」

sources.en: Stroke order of 日 (4 strokes): vertical, horizontal-turn-hook, the middle horizontal, the bottom horizontal
sources.zh: 「日」4 畫：豎、橫折鉤、橫、橫（封口）
sources.src: 教育部《國字標準字體筆順學習網》「日」

units.blurb_en: From marks on tortoise shells to the neat lines of seal script, the silkworm heads and swallow tails of clerical script, and the speed of running and cursive script.
units.blurb_zh: 從龜甲上的刻痕到線條勻稱的篆書、蠶頭燕尾的隸書，再到越寫越快的行書與草書。

lessons.title: Where Did Chinese Characters Come From?
lessons.title_zh: 漢字從哪裡來？甲骨文到篆書
lessons.blurb_en: Long before paper, people carved characters on tortoise shells and cast them in bronze. In 3D, crack a shell the way Shang diviners did, carve a character, make a rubbing from a bronze ding, and watch a brush write small seal script. Then pull a slider through 3,000 years.
lessons.blurb_zh: 在有紙以前，人們把字刻在龜甲上、鑄在青銅器上。在 3D 裡照商代占卜的方法讓龜甲裂開、刻一個字，從青銅鼎拓下銘文，再看毛筆寫小篆；最後拉一根滑桿，走過三千年。
lessons.big_idea_en: The earliest Chinese writing that survives on real objects was carved on tortoise shells and animal bones more than 3,000 years ago. Many of those characters began as pictures of things. Over many centuries, the shapes became simpler and more even: carved oracle bone script, bronze script, and then small seal script, the standard of the Qin dynasty.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 現存有實物可證的最早漢字，是三千多年前刻在龜甲、獸骨上的甲骨文；其中許多字一開始是東西的圖畫。經過很多個世紀，字形越來越簡單、線條越來越勻稱：刀刻的甲骨文、青銅器上的金文，再到秦朝的標準字體小篆。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Choose where the writing is made: on a tortoise shell, in a bronze ding, or with a brush. Choose one of six characters, and each place shows it in that time's script. On the shell, follow four steps: hollows, heat, crack, and carve.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。選字寫在哪裡：龜甲上、青銅鼎裡，或用毛筆寫；再選六個字中的一個，每個地方都用那個時代的字形。在龜甲上可以一步一步看：挖洞、灼燒、裂開、刻字。

modes.title_en: Ask a question, read the crack
modes.text_en: Diviners cut hollows into the back of a tortoise shell and heated them. Cracks appeared on the front, and the record was carved beside them.
modes.text_zh: 占卜的人在龜甲背面挖凹洞、用火燒，正面就出現裂紋；占卜的紀錄刻在裂紋旁邊。

steps.en: Hollows
steps.zh: 鑽鑿
steps.text_en: Hollows are cut into the back of the shell. They make the shell thinner there, so a crack can form when it is heated.
steps.text_zh: 在龜甲背面挖出凹洞（鑽鑿），讓那裡變薄，加熱時才容易裂開。

steps.en: Heat
steps.zh: 灼燒
steps.text_en: The red-hot end of a wooden stick is pressed into a hollow on the back.
steps.text_zh: 用燒紅的木條末端，去燒背面挖好的凹洞。

steps.en: Crack
steps.zh: 卜兆
steps.text_en: With a cracking sound, a crack appears on the front, shaped a bit like 卜. One scholar suggested that 卜 copies both the sound and the shape of the crack. Nobody today knows exactly how the diviners read the cracks.
steps.text_zh: 甲骨發出裂開的聲音，正面出現像「卜」字的裂紋（卜兆）。有學者說，「卜」字既模仿裂開的聲音，也畫出裂紋的樣子。古人到底怎麼判讀裂紋，現在已經不可考。

steps.en: Carve
steps.zh: 刻字
steps.text_en: The record is carved with a knife beside the crack: the date, who asked, the question, and the answer. Knife lines are thin and straight; carve 日 and see how the round sun comes out almost square.
steps.text_zh: 用刀把紀錄刻在裂紋旁邊：哪一天、誰來問、問什麼、得到什麼答案。刀刻的線又細又直；刻刻看「日」，圓圓的太陽刻出來幾乎是方的。

modes.text_en: In the Shang and Zhou dynasties, writing was cast or carved on bronze vessels like this ding. A rubbing turns it into a page: paper is pressed onto the writing and patted with ink, and the sunken lines stay white.
modes.text_zh: 商周時代，字鑄或刻在青銅器上，像這個鼎。拓片把它變成一張紙：紙貼在字上、拍上墨，凹下去的筆畫就留白。

modes.text_en: After the Qin dynasty united China in 221 BCE, small seal script became the standard. Its lines are smooth and the same width, so a brush keeps its tip in the middle and presses evenly all the way.
modes.text_zh: 秦在西元前 221 年統一天下以後，小篆成為標準字體。線條圓滑、粗細一樣，所以毛筆用中鋒、從頭到尾力道平均。

legend.en: Bone-colored shell: a tortoise plastron, the underside of the shell
legend.zh: 米黃色：龜的腹甲（龜殼的腹面）

legend.en: Green metal: a bronze ding with three legs
legend.zh: 綠色金屬：三隻腳的青銅鼎

lab.scale_en: A teaching model, not to scale: real oracle bone characters are much smaller, and a real ding is much bigger. In the model, the inscription sits on the bottom of the bowl so it is easy to see. The character forms are our own tracings over public domain reference glyphs.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型，不照實際比例：真的甲骨文字小得多，真的鼎大得多。模型把銘文放在鼎的內底，比較容易看。字形是我們對著公有領域的參考字形自己描的。
lab.credit_html: Model, character tracings, and the writing engine are drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect. Reference glyphs for the oracle bone, bronze, and seal scripts: Wikimedia Commons, Ancient Chinese Characters Project (public domain). · 模型、字形描線與寫字引擎由人師教育協會自繪、自寫；甲骨文、金文、小篆的對位參考是 Wikimedia Commons「Ancient Chinese characters project」的公有領域字形。

paras: Before there was paper, people in China wrote on hard things. More than 3,000 years ago, in the late Shang dynasty, people carved characters on tortoise shells and animal bones, mostly the shoulder blades of cattle. We call this writing oracle bone script. Taiwan's Ministry of Education calls it the earliest Chinese writing that survives on real objects.

Why carve on shells? The Shang kings asked many questions about what would happen. Diviners cut hollows into the back of a shell or bone and pressed the red-hot end of a wooden stick into them. Cracks appeared on the front, shaped a bit like the character 卜, which means to divine. Then they carved the record beside the cracks: the date, the question, and the answer. Nobody today knows exactly how they read the cracks.

Many early characters began as pictures of things. 日 was the sun, 月 a crescent moon, 山 three mountain peaks, 水 a stream with drops of water, 人 a person seen from the side, and 馬 a horse standing on its tail, with a big eye and a mane. About 1,900 years ago, the scholar Xu Shen called this way of making characters 象形, drawing the shape of a thing, and he gave 日 and 月 as his examples.

Writing was also cast or carved on bronze. In the Shang and Zhou dynasties, words were put on bronze vessels such as the ding, a pot with three legs. These lines are thicker and rounder than carved lines. To study them on paper, people make rubbings: paper is pressed onto the writing and patted with ink, and the sunken characters stay white. The Mao Gong Ding in the National Palace Museum in Taipei holds about 500 characters in 32 lines.

In 221 BCE, the state of Qin united China. The Shiji, a famous history, records that the First Emperor made the writing the same everywhere. Li Si and other officials simplified the older script into a standard form called small seal script, with smooth lines of even width.

After seal script came clerical script, flat and wide (Lesson 6), and then regular script, the way we write today (Lesson 7). In this lesson, crack and carve a shell in 3D, make a rubbing from a bronze ding, and watch a brush write seal script. Then pull the slider to see one character change over 3,000 years.
paras_zh: 在有紙以前，中國人把字寫在硬的東西上。三千多年前的商代晚期，人們把字刻在龜甲和獸骨（大多是牛的肩胛骨）上，我們叫它甲骨文。台灣教育部的辭典說，甲骨文是中國有實物可證的最早文字。
為什麼要刻在龜甲上？商王對未來有很多問題。占卜的人在龜甲或獸骨的背面挖出凹洞，再用燒紅的木條末端去燒，正面就出現裂紋，形狀有點像「卜」字，「卜」就是占卜的意思。接著，他們把紀錄刻在裂紋旁邊：哪一天、問什麼、得到什麼答案。古人到底怎麼判讀裂紋，現在已經不可考了。
許多早期的字是從東西的圖畫來的：「日」是太陽，「月」是彎彎的月亮，「山」是三座山峰，「水」是一道水流和兩旁的水滴，「人」是側面的人，「馬」是一匹站起來的馬，有大眼睛和鬃毛。大約一千九百年前，學者許慎把這種造字方法叫做「象形」，也就是照著東西的樣子畫出來，他舉的例子正是「日」和「月」。
字也鑄或刻在青銅器上。商周時代，人們把文字放在鼎這類青銅器上；鼎是有三隻腳的鍋子。這些線條比刻的線粗、也比較圓。為了在紙上研究，人們做拓片：把紙貼在字上、拍上墨，凹下去的字就留白。台北國立故宮博物院的毛公鼎，裡面有 32 行、大約 500 個字。
西元前 221 年，秦統一天下。著名的史書《史記》記載，秦始皇讓全國「書同文字」。李斯等官員把舊的字體加以省改，成為標準字體，叫做小篆，線條圓滑、粗細一樣。
小篆之後是字形扁扁的隸書（第六課），再來是我們今天寫的楷書（第七課）。這一課，在 3D 裡讓龜甲裂開、刻一個字，從青銅鼎拓下銘文，看毛筆寫小篆；再拉動滑桿，看一個字三千年來怎麼變。
questions: What did people in the late Shang dynasty carve characters on?
How did the diviners make cracks appear on a shell?
What does 象形 mean, and which two characters did Xu Shen give as examples?
answers: They carved characters on tortoise shells and animal bones.
They cut hollows into the back and pressed the red-hot end of a wooden stick into them. Cracks appeared on the front.
It means drawing the shape of a thing. His examples were 日 and 月.

vocab.ex: The ancient city is more than 2,000 years old.
vocab.exzh: 這座古城已經兩千多年了。

vocab.ex: She carved a small bird out of soap.
vocab.exzh: 她用肥皂刻了一隻小鳥。

vocab.ex: There is a long crack in the window.
vocab.exzh: 窗戶上有一條長長的裂縫。

vocab.ex: The turtle hid its head inside its shell.
vocab.exzh: 烏龜把頭縮進殼裡。

vocab.ex: The statue in the park is made of bronze.
vocab.exzh: 公園裡的雕像是青銅做的。

vocab.ex: The workers cast the bell from hot metal.
vocab.exzh: 工人用熔化的金屬鑄成這口鐘。

vocab.ex: A heart is a symbol of love.
vocab.exzh: 愛心是愛的象徵。

vocab.ex: The two teams united to clean the beach.
vocab.exzh: 兩隊聯合起來打掃海灘。

quiz.q: How was oracle bone script made?
options: It was carved on shells and bones.

quiz.q: Which character looks like a crack in a shell?
Where is the Mao Gong Ding today?

parts.text_en: A sun with a mark in the middle. Carved on bone, the circle is made of straight lines and looks almost square. Cast in bronze, it is round again, with a fat dot. In seal script, the dot becomes a line across.
parts.text_zh: 中間有一點的太陽。刻在骨頭上，圓圈用直線刻，看起來幾乎是方的；鑄在青銅上又變圓了，中間是一個胖胖的點；到了小篆，那一點變成一橫。

parts.text_en: A crescent moon. The oracle bone form is a curved slice; later forms add lines inside, and the crescent slowly turns into the 月 we write today.
parts.text_zh: 彎彎的月亮。甲骨文是一片彎彎的月牙；後來裡面多了線條，月牙慢慢變成今天寫的「月」。

parts.text_en: Three peaks standing on the ground, with the middle one the tallest. The peaks became three vertical strokes on a base.
parts.text_zh: 三座山峰站在地上，中間那座最高。山峰後來變成三豎，站在一條底線上。

parts.text_en: A stream in the middle with drops of water on both sides. In regular script, the drops became the strokes on the left and right.
parts.text_zh: 中間一道水流，兩旁是水滴。到了楷書，水滴變成左右兩邊的筆畫。

parts.text_en: A person seen from the side, bending forward with an arm hanging down. Two strokes are left in 人.
parts.text_zh: 從側面看的人，身體往前彎、手垂下來。到了「人」字，只剩下兩筆。

parts.text_en: A horse standing on its tail: a big eye at the top, a mane along the back, and legs on the left. The Shuowen says 馬 shows the horse's head, mane, tail, and four legs.
parts.text_zh: 一匹站起來的馬：上面是大眼睛，背上有鬃毛，腿在左邊。《說文解字》說「馬」字畫的是馬的頭、鬃毛、尾巴和四隻腳。

lessons.parts_note_en: Each card shows one character in four scripts: oracle bone, bronze, small seal, and regular. Tap Watch it in 3D to see it carved, cast, and written.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 每張卡片用四種字體畫同一個字：甲骨文、金文、小篆、楷書。點「在模型中看」，看它被刻、被鑄、被寫出來。

time.en: Three thousand years in one slider
time.lead_en: Choose a character and pull the slider. Watch it change from a picture to oracle bone script, bronze script, small seal script, clerical script, and the regular script we write today.
time.lead_zh: 選一個字，拉動滑桿：看它從圖畫變成甲骨文、金文、小篆、隸書，一直到我們今天寫的楷書。

stages.text_en: Many early characters began as pictures of things. These pictures are our own drawings, made to show the idea.
stages.text_zh: 許多早期的字是從東西的圖畫來的。這裡的圖是我們畫的示意圖，方便看懂這個想法。

stages.text_en: Carved with a knife on shells and bones, so the lines are thin and straight. Look at the horse: it stands on its tail, with its head at the top.
stages.text_zh: 用刀刻在龜甲、獸骨上，線條又細又直。看看那匹馬：牠站起來了，頭在上面。

stages.text_en: Cast or carved on bronze vessels. The lines are thicker and rounder. Here it is shown as a rubbing: white on black.
stages.text_zh: 鑄或刻在青銅器上，線條比較粗、比較圓。這裡畫成拓片：黑底白字。

stages.text_en: The standard script after the Qin dynasty united China. The lines are smooth and the same width everywhere.
stages.text_zh: 秦統一天下後的標準字體。線條圓滑，每一處都一樣粗。

stages.when_en: Began in the Qin, common in the Han and Wei
stages.text_en: A simpler form of seal script. The shapes become flat and wide, and curves become straight lines and turns. Our drawing is a sketch; Lesson 6 looks closer.
stages.text_zh: 篆書的簡化體。字形變扁、變寬，彎彎的線變成直線和轉折。這裡畫的是示意，第六課再仔細看。

stages.when_en: Complete by the Wei, still used today
stages.text_en: Regular script grew out of clerical script and is still used today. This is the form you learn in school.
stages.text_zh: 楷書由隸書演變而來，一直用到今天，就是我們在學校學的字。

which.lead_en: Look at an oracle bone character and choose the modern character. A wrong answer gives you a clue. When you are ready, try the bronze script.
which.lead_zh: 看一個甲骨文，選出今天的字。答錯了會有提示。熟練以後，換金文試試看。

ri.en: Look for a shape with a mark in the middle. What shines in the sky all day?
ri.zh: 找一個中間有一點的形狀。白天在天上發光的是什麼？

yue.en: It is a curved shape like a slice. What do you see in the sky at night?
yue.zh: 它是彎彎的一片。晚上在天上看到的是什麼？

shan.en: Count the points on top. What would you climb?
shan.zh: 數數上面有幾個尖尖。你會去爬的是什麼？

shui.en: One wavy line in the middle with drops on both sides. What flows?
shui.zh: 中間一條彎彎的線，兩邊有水滴。什麼東西會流？

ren.en: It has a back and an arm. Who could it be?

ma.en: Find a big eye, a mane, and legs. This animal is standing on its tail.
ma.zh: 找找大眼睛、鬃毛和腿。這隻動物站起來了。

pad.lead_en: Choose a character and trace its small seal script. Seal lines stay the same width, so keep an even, steady speed. After each stroke, the chart compares your press-and-lift curve with the brush's flat one.
pad.lead_zh: 選一個字，描寫它的小篆。小篆的線粗細一樣，所以速度要平穩、不快不慢。每寫完一筆，圖上就把你的提按曲線和毛筆平平的曲線比較。

tips.en: Keep the same speed from the start of a line to the end: slow and steady.
tips.zh: 一條線從頭到尾保持同樣的速度：慢慢地、穩穩地。

tips.en: Start and finish each line with a round end, not a point.
tips.zh: 每條線的頭和尾都是圓的，不要尖尖的。

tips.en: Turn slowly around the curves, like the bottom of 日 and 山.
tips.zh: 轉彎的地方慢慢轉，像「日」和「山」的底部。

links_head.eyebrow: Before and Next · 上一課與下一課
links_head.en: From stroke order to clerical script

links.en: Why Do We Write Strokes in Order?
links.zh: 筆順與結構：為什麼要先橫後豎？
links.note_en: Today's standard stroke order belongs to regular script, the last stage on this lesson's slider.
links.note_zh: 今天的標準筆順是楷書的筆順，也就是這一課滑桿的最後一站。

links.en: Why Does Clerical Script Have Silkworm Heads and Swallow Tails?
links.zh: 隸書：為什麼是蠶頭燕尾？
links.note_en: Clerical script made seal script simpler: the shapes became flat and wide, and the horizontal stroke grew a head like a silkworm and a tail that flicks up.
links.note_zh: 隸書把小篆簡化了：字形變得扁扁寬寬，橫畫起筆像蠶頭、收筆往上挑出尾巴。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories of Ancient Writing · 古文字的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A medicine with writing, fifteen digs, the longest inscription, and an old dictionary
culture_cards.title_zh: 藥材上的字、十五次發掘、最長的銘文，和一本古老的字典
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about how we found, kept, and explained the oldest Chinese writing.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於最古老的漢字怎麼被發現、被保存、被解釋的四個小故事。

cards.body_en: Oracle bones came from Xiaotun village near Anyang, Henan, and 1899 is usually given as the year they were discovered. A famous story says the scholar Wang Yirong was ill, and writing was spotted on a piece of turtle shell bought as medicine. Historians have shown that this story cannot be trusted; another account says an antique dealer brought Wang twelve pieces. Wang died in 1900, and in 1903 Liu E published the first book of oracle bone rubbings.
cards.body_zh: 甲骨出自河南安陽附近的小屯村，後人通常把 1899 年當作甲骨文發現的年份。有個有名的故事說，學者王懿榮生病，有人在買來當藥的龜版上看見了字；學者已經證明這個故事不可信。另一種說法是古董商帶了十二片甲骨給王懿榮看。王懿榮 1900 年就去世了，1903 年劉鶚出版了第一本甲骨拓片的書《鐵雲藏龜》。

cards.body_en: From 1928 to 1937, Academia Sinica's Institute of History and Philology dug fifteen times at Yinxu, the ruins of the late Shang capital near Anyang. Today the institute in Taipei holds more than 25,000 pieces of oracle bones, and its museum shows some of them. In 2006, Yinxu became a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
cards.body_zh: 1928 到 1937 年，中央研究院歷史語言研究所在安陽附近的殷墟（商代晚期的都城遺址）進行了十五次發掘。現在位在台北的史語所收藏了兩萬五千多片甲骨，所裡的歷史文物陳列館可以看到其中一些。2006 年，殷墟列入聯合國教科文組織的世界遺產。

cards.k: The Longest Inscription · 最長的銘文
cards.en: The Mao Gong Ding in Taipei
cards.body_en: The Mao Gong Ding is a bronze ding from the late Western Zhou dynasty. Inside its bowl are 32 lines of writing, about 500 characters. The National Palace Museum in Taipei calls it the longest bronze inscription known so far. The Ministry of Education's dictionary counts 497 characters, so we say about 500.
cards.body_zh: 毛公鼎是西周晚期的青銅鼎，鼎腹裡面鑄了 32 行字，大約 500 字。台北國立故宮博物院說它是目前所知最長的青銅器銘文。教育部辭典算的是 497 字，所以我們說「大約 500 字」。

cards.body_en: Around the year 100, the scholar Xu Shen finished the Shuowen Jiezi. It explains 9,353 characters, written in small seal script and sorted into 540 groups. It describes six ways characters were made; drawing the shape of a thing (象形) is one of them, with 日 and 月 as examples. It also says 卜 shows the shape of a heated shell's crack.
cards.body_zh: 大約西元 100 年，東漢學者許慎完成了《說文解字》，用小篆解說 9,353 個字，分成 540 部。書裡說造字的方法有六種（六書），「象形」是其中一種，例子是「日」和「月」；書裡也說「卜」字像燒過的龜甲上的裂紋。

myths.myth_en: Every Chinese character is a picture.
myths.myth_zh: 每個漢字都是一幅畫。
myths.fact_en: Only some began as pictures. Xu Shen described six ways characters were made. Many characters join a part for meaning with a part for sound, like 江 and 河, his own examples.
myths.fact_zh: 只有一部分是從圖畫來的。許慎說造字有六種方法；很多字是「表示意思的部分」加上「表示讀音的部分」，像他舉的「江」和「河」。

myths.myth_en: One man, Cangjie, invented Chinese writing.
myths.myth_zh: 漢字是倉頡一個人發明的。
myths.fact_en: That is a legend. As the Ministry of Education's dictionary says, writing could not be invented by one person; it grew little by little over a long time.
myths.fact_zh: 那是傳說。教育部辭典說，文字不可能是一個人獨創的，而是先人一點一點累積而成。

myths.myth_en: Scholars can read every oracle bone character.
myths.myth_zh: 學者已經看得懂所有的甲骨文。
myths.fact_en: Not yet. A 2016 UNESCO report counts about 4,400 different characters, and only about 1,400 of them match characters we use today. Other counts differ a little, but many are still a puzzle.
myths.fact_zh: 還沒有。2016 年聯合國教科文組織的報告說，甲骨文大約有 4,400 個不同的字，其中大約只有 1,400 個對得上今天用的字。各家的數字有些不同，但還有很多字是謎。

myths.myth_en: Ancient characters look nothing like today's.
myths.myth_zh: 古文字和今天的字完全不像。
myths.fact_en: Many keep their shape. 山 still has three peaks, 水 still has a stream in the middle, and 人 still has two strokes. Pull the slider and look for what stays the same.
myths.fact_zh: 很多字保留了原來的樣子：「山」還是三座山峰，「水」中間還是一道水流，「人」還是兩筆。拉拉看滑桿，找找什麼沒有變。

tricks.body_en: Oracle bones were carved, bronze was cast, and seal script has even lines.
tricks.body_zh: 甲骨文用刀刻，金文在青銅器上，小篆線條勻稱。

tricks.body_en: One line down and one line out, like the crack on a shell.
tricks.body_zh: 一豎一點，就像龜甲上的裂紋。

tricks.title_en: 日 and 月 are pictures
tricks.body_en: Xu Shen's examples of drawing the shape of a thing.
tricks.body_zh: 許慎舉的象形字例子。

tricks.body_en: Qin united China and made the writing the same.
tricks.body_zh: 秦統一天下，全國的字寫成一樣。

safety.en: Carve with a blunt wooden stick or a dull pencil on clay or a foam tray. Never use a real knife in class.
safety.zh: 用鈍的木棒或沒削尖的鉛筆，在黏土或保麗龍盤上刻；上課時絕對不要用真的刀。

safety.en: Do not try to crack shells or bones with heat. The model shows how it was done; we do not do it in class.
safety.zh: 不要自己用火燒龜甲或骨頭。模型示範古人怎麼做，課堂上不做。

safety.en: Crayons and ink can stain. Cover the desk and wear old clothes or an apron.
safety.zh: 蠟筆和墨都會弄髒：桌上先鋪報紙，穿舊衣服或圍裙。

safety.en: Wash your hands after working with clay, crayons, or ink.
safety.zh: 玩過黏土、蠟筆或墨之後，記得洗手。

materials.en: A flat piece of clay for each student (or a clean foam tray)
materials.zh: 每人一塊壓平的黏土（或一個洗乾淨的保麗龍盤）

materials.en: A blunt wooden stick or a dull pencil
materials.zh: 一根鈍的木棒，或沒削尖的鉛筆

materials.en: A sheet with the six oracle bone characters from this lesson
materials.zh: 一張印好這一課六個甲骨文的學習單

steps.en: Shape the clay like a shell or a bone, and press it flat.
steps.zh: 把黏土捏成龜甲或骨頭的形狀，再壓平。

steps.en: On the left, carve a crack shaped like 卜.
steps.zh: 在左邊刻一個像「卜」的裂紋。

steps.en: Beside the crack, carve one of the six oracle bone characters using only straight lines.
steps.zh: 在裂紋旁邊刻六個甲骨文中的一個，只能用直線。

steps.en: Trade with a classmate. Can they read your character? Can you read theirs?
steps.zh: 和同學交換：他看得出你刻的是什麼字嗎？你看得出他的嗎？

activities.tip_en: Ask the class: was it harder to carve a circle or a straight line? Then look at 日 in oracle bone script.
activities.tip_zh: 問問全班：刻圓圈和刻直線，哪個比較難？再看看甲骨文的「日」。

materials.en: A clean foam tray
materials.zh: 一個洗乾淨的保麗龍盤

materials.en: A pencil, thin paper, and a crayon with the paper peeled off
materials.zh: 一枝鉛筆、一張薄紙，和一枝剝掉包裝紙的蠟筆

steps.en: Press hard with the pencil to draw a character into the foam, so the lines sink in.
steps.zh: 用鉛筆用力在保麗龍盤上寫一個字，讓筆畫凹下去。

steps.en: Lay the paper on top and hold it still.
steps.zh: 把薄紙蓋在上面，按好不要動。

steps.en: Rub the side of the crayon across the paper. The sunken lines stay white.
steps.zh: 用蠟筆的側面在紙上來回塗，凹下去的筆畫就留白了。

steps.en: Compare your rubbing with the one in the 3D model.
steps.zh: 把你的拓片和 3D 模型裡的拓片比一比。

activities.tip_en: Try 日 in bronze script: a circle with a fat dot in the middle.
activities.tip_zh: 試試金文的「日」：一個圓圈，中間一個胖胖的點。

sources.en: Oracle bone script: carved on tortoise shells and animal bones for divination in the Shang dynasty; the earliest Chinese writing proven by real objects; found at Xiaotun, Anyang, from 1899
sources.zh: 甲骨文：商代人占卜時刻於龜甲、獸骨上的文字，為中國有實物可證的最早文字；光緒二十五年在河南安陽小屯村陸續發現
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「甲骨文」

sources.en: Oracle bones discovered in 1899; the institute holds more than 25,000 pieces
sources.zh: 甲骨文自一八九九年發現；本所現藏甲骨二萬五千多片
sources.src: 中央研究院歷史語言研究所歷史文物陳列館〈甲骨〉

sources.en: Fifteen seasons of excavation at Yinxu, 1928 to 1937
sources.zh: 1928 至 1937 年在殷墟進行十五次發掘
sources.src: Institute of History and Philology Museum, Academia Sinica

sources.en: How divination worked: mostly tortoise shells and cattle shoulder blades; hollows (鑽鑿) to thin the shell; a red-hot stick; a cracking sound and a crack like 卜 (Chen Mengjia on 卜); records of date, person, question, and result; how the cracks were read is no longer known
sources.zh: 龜甲與獸骨（以牛肩胛骨佔多數）；鑽鑿使甲骨變薄；燒紅的木條燋灼；「卜」聲與類似「卜」字的裂紋（陳夢家說）；刻下時間、人物、問題、吉凶與應驗；如何判斷已不可考
sources.src: 中研院史語所歷史文物陳列館〈殷商占卜的取材與過程〉

sources.en: The Wang Yirong medicine story cannot be trusted; 1899 is the year later given for the discovery (Li Zongkun, 2008)
sources.zh: 王懿榮從藥材發現甲骨的說法不可信；後人以 1899 年為甲骨文發現之年（李宗焜，《古今論衡》第 18 期，2008）
sources.src: 中央研究院歷史語言研究所《古今論衡》

sources.en: Wang Yirong: the medicine story (“據說”), the dealer with twelve pieces, his death in 1900, and Liu E's 1903 book of rubbings
sources.zh: 王懿榮：「據說」的藥材故事、古董商帶十二片甲骨的另一種說法、1900 年去世、劉鶚 1903 年《鐵雲藏龜》
sources.src: 中央研究院「商王陵」網站〈王懿榮〉

sources.en: Yin Xu: near Anyang, Henan; capital of the late Shang dynasty (1300–1046 BC); inscribed in 2006
sources.zh: 殷墟：河南安陽附近，商代晚期都城（西元前 1300–1046 年）；2006 年列入世界遺產
sources.src: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, “Yin Xu”

sources.en: Chinese Oracle-Bone Inscriptions in the Memory of the World Register (2017); nomination counts about 150,000 pieces, about 4,400 characters, about 1,400 matching modern characters
sources.zh: 甲骨文 2017 年列入世界記憶名錄；申報書：約十五萬片、約四千四百字、約一千四百字可對應今字
sources.src: UNESCO Memory of the World

sources.en: Shuowen on 卜: “灼剥龜也，象炙龜之形。一曰象龜兆之從橫也”
sources.zh: 《說文解字》卷三下「卜」（四部叢刊本）
sources.src: 維基文庫《說文解字》（四部叢刊本）卷第三下

sources.en: Shuowen postface: six ways of making characters; 象形 with 日 and 月 as examples; 形聲 with 江 and 河; 540 groups and 9,353 characters; Li Si and small seal script
sources.zh: 《說文解字．敘》：六書、「象形者，畫成其物，隨體詰詘，日、月是也」、形聲「江、河」、五百四十部、九千三百五十三文、李斯與小篆
sources.src: 維基文庫《說文解字》卷十五

sources.en: Shuowen on 馬: shows the horse's head, mane, tail, and four legs
sources.zh: 《說文解字》「馬」：象馬頭髦尾四足之形
sources.src: 維基文庫《說文解字》卷十

sources.en: Shuowen Jiezi by Xu Shen of the Eastern Han: 540 groups, 9,353 characters
sources.zh: 《說文解字》：東漢許慎撰，分列五百四十部，收錄九千三百五十三字
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「說文解字」

sources.en: Bronze inscriptions: writing cast or carved on bronze vessels from the Shang to the Han
sources.zh: 金文：商周秦漢時代鑄刻在青銅器上的文字
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「金文」

sources.en: Mao Gong Ding: late Western Zhou; 500 characters, the longest bronze inscription known so far
sources.zh: 毛公鼎：西周晚期；銘文全長五百字，為迄今所知最長的青銅器銘文
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院〈毛公鼎〉

sources.en: Mao Gong Ding: 497 characters
sources.zh: 毛公鼎：四百九十七字
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「毛公鼎」

sources.en: Shiji, Annals of the First Emperor: “書同文字” (221 BCE)
sources.zh: 《史記．秦始皇本紀》：「一法度衡石丈尺。車同軌。書同文字。」
sources.src: 維基文庫《史記》卷六

sources.en: Small seal script: after Qin united China, Li Si and others simplified the great seal script into the official standard
sources.zh: 小篆：秦統一天下後，令李斯等人在大篆的基礎上加以省改，頒行全國成為官定的標準字體
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「小篆」

sources.en: 象形: one of the six ways, drawing the shape of a thing
sources.zh: 象形：六書之一，根據物體的形象描繪而成文字
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「象形」

sources.en: Cangjie: said to be the inventor of writing, but writing could not be invented by one person
sources.zh: 倉頡：相傳為漢字的創造者，然文字不可能是一人所獨創
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「倉頡」

sources.en: Clerical script: a simpler form of seal script, begun in the Qin and common in the Han and Wei
sources.zh: 隸書：篆書的簡化體，創始於秦，通行於漢、魏
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「隸書」

sources.en: Regular script: grew out of clerical script, complete by the Wei, still used today
sources.zh: 楷書：由隸書演變而來，約起源於後漢，至魏完備成體，通行至今
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「楷書」

sources.en: Rubbing: a sheet made by copying writing or pictures from steles and bronzes
sources.zh: 拓片：將碑刻、金石文物上的字畫拓印下來的紙片
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「拓片」

sources.en: Stroke order of 月 (4 strokes), 山 (3), 水 (4), and 馬 (10) for the regular-script drawings
sources.zh: 楷書範字「月」4 畫、「山」3 畫、「水」4 畫、「馬」10 畫的筆順
sources.src: 教育部《國字標準字體筆順學習網》

sources.zh: 甲骨文、金文、小篆描線的對位參考字形（公有領域）

lessons.title: Why Does Clerical Script Have Silkworm Heads and Swallow Tails?
lessons.title_zh: 隸書：為什麼是蠶頭燕尾？
lessons.blurb_en: Clerical script made writing quicker: curves became straight lines, tall shapes became flat, and one stroke in each character got a head like a silkworm's and a tail like a swallow's. Watch a 3D brush write that stroke part by part, see seal script turn into clerical script, and unroll a scroll of bamboo slips.
lessons.blurb_zh: 隸書讓寫字變快了：彎彎的線變直、長長的字形變扁，每個字有一筆起筆像蠶頭、收筆像燕尾。看 3D 毛筆一段一段寫出這一筆，看小篆變成隸書，再攤開一卷竹簡。
lessons.big_idea_en: Clerical script is a simpler form of seal script, made to be quick to write. It began in the Qin dynasty and was the common script of the Han dynasty. Its shapes are flat and wide, its curves have become straight lines and turns, and its long horizontal stroke begins like a silkworm's head and ends like a swallow's tail.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 隸書是篆書的簡化體，為了寫得快而出現。它創始於秦、通行於漢。字形扁而寬，彎曲的線變成直線和轉折；長長的橫畫，起筆像蠶頭、收筆像燕尾。

lab.title_en: One Stroke, One Change, One Scroll
lab.how_en: Drag to turn, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Watch the brush write the long horizontal stroke, and replay its head, middle, and tail in slow motion. Then choose The change to see seal script turn into clerical script, or Bamboo slips to unroll a scroll and write on it.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。看毛筆寫出長長的橫畫，蠶頭、行筆、燕尾三段都能慢動作重播。再選「隸變」看小篆變成隸書，或選「竹簡」攤開一卷竹簡、在上面寫字。

modes.title_en: A silkworm head and a swallow tail
modes.text_en: The brush goes in backward, turns, and travels to the right. Near the end it presses down, then flicks up to the right. Replay each part in slow motion, or compare it with the horizontal stroke of regular script, which ends without a flick.
modes.text_zh: 毛筆先逆著往左入紙、回鋒，再往右走；快到尾巴時往下按，再往右上挑出去。每一段都可以慢動作重播；也可以和楷書的橫比一比——楷書收筆不往上挑。

modes.title_en: From seal script to clerical script
modes.text_en: The faint blue character is small seal script. The brush writes the same character in clerical script on top of it: round turns become square corners, and the tall shape becomes flat.
modes.text_zh: 淡藍色的是小篆。毛筆在同一個格子裡寫出隸書：圓圓的轉彎變成方方的轉角，長長的字形變扁了。

modes.text_en: In the Qin and Han dynasties, people wrote with a brush on narrow slips of bamboo or wood, from top to bottom, and tied the slips together with cords to make a book. Slips tied like this can be rolled up. The character 冊 is a picture of slips tied with two cords.
modes.text_zh: 秦漢時代，人們用毛筆在窄窄的竹片或木片上由上往下寫字，再用繩子把一片片編成一冊；編好的簡可以捲起來。「冊」這個字，畫的就是用兩道繩子編起來的簡。

parts.text_en: The start: the brush touches down moving left, presses, and turns back to the right. The hidden turn makes a round head, like a silkworm's.
parts.text_zh: 起筆：筆尖先往左入紙、按下去，再回過頭往右走。這個藏起來的回鋒，讓起筆圓圓鼓起來，像蠶的頭。

parts.text_en: The middle: the brush travels to the right with steady pressure.
parts.text_zh: 行筆：毛筆用平穩的力道往右走。

parts.text_en: The end: the brush presses down, then lifts as it flicks up to the right. The Ministry of Education's dictionary calls it a wild goose's tail (雁尾); many people say swallow tail (燕尾).
parts.text_zh: 收筆：毛筆先往下頓、再一邊提起一邊往右上挑出去。教育部辭典說它像「雁尾」，很多人說「燕尾」。

legend.en: Faint blue lines: the same character in small seal script
legend.zh: 淡藍色的線：同一個字的小篆

legend.en: Bamboo slips tied with two cords
legend.zh: 用兩道繩子編起來的竹簡

legend.en: Yellow labels: names of the parts
legend.zh: 黃色標籤：各部分的名稱

legend.en: Red lines: the 米 grid
legend.zh: 紅線：米字格

lab.scale_en: A teaching model, not to scale: the slips and the characters on them are enlarged. The clerical characters are our own sketches in the style of Han clerical script, with one swallow tail in each character; the stroke order follows today's regular script.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型，不照實際比例：竹簡和上面的字都放大了。隸書的字是我們照漢代隸書的典型寫法自己畫的示意，每個字只有一個燕尾；筆順照今天楷書的筆順。
lab.credit_html: Model, stroke data, and the writing engine are drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect. The seal-script forms are our own tracings over public domain reference glyphs (Wikimedia Commons, Ancient Chinese Characters Project). · 模型、筆畫資料與寫字引擎由人師教育協會自繪、自寫；小篆是對著 Wikimedia Commons 公有領域的參考字形自己描的。

paras: Small seal script looks neat, with smooth, even lines, but it takes time to write. Xu Shen, a scholar of the Han dynasty, wrote that in the Qin dynasty the government offices and prisons had so much work that a new kind of writing appeared to make things quick and simple. That writing was clerical script.

Clerical script changed the shapes of characters. Round turns became square corners. Long curves became straight lines. Characters that stood tall in seal script became flat and wide. This change is called libian (隸變), and after it, characters began to look like the ones we write today.

The most famous clerical stroke is the long horizontal line. It starts with a silkworm head: the brush touches down moving backward, then turns and travels to the right, so the start looks round. It ends with a swallow tail: the brush presses down, then lifts as it flicks up to the right.

A clerical character usually has only one swallow tail. Look at 三: only the long bottom line has a tail, and the two lines above end round. Later calligraphers summed up this habit in a saying: wild geese do not fly in pairs, and a silkworm head is not set down twice.

Clerical script was the common script of the Han dynasty. People wrote it with a brush on narrow slips of bamboo and wood, and tied the slips together with cords to make a book. More than 10,000 Han dynasty slips were found near Juyan, on the northwest frontier, in 1930 and 1931. Today they are kept at Academia Sinica in Taipei.

In this lesson, replay the three parts of the long horizontal stroke in 3D, watch seal script change into clerical script, and unroll a scroll of bamboo slips. Then drag the line between the two scripts, find the swallow tails, and trace the strokes yourself.
paras_zh: 小篆看起來很整齊，線條圓滑、粗細一樣，可是寫起來很花時間。東漢學者許慎說，秦代官府和監獄的事務太多了，於是出現一種新的字體，讓書寫又快又簡單——那就是隸書。
隸書改變了字的樣子：圓圓的轉彎變成方方的轉角，長長的彎線變成直線，小篆裡高高的字形變得又扁又寬。這個變化叫做「隸變」；隸變之後，漢字開始像我們今天寫的樣子。
隸書最有名的一筆是長長的橫畫。起筆是「蠶頭」：筆尖先逆著入紙，再回過頭往右走，所以起筆是圓的。收筆是「燕尾」：毛筆先往下按，再一邊提起、一邊往右上挑出去。
一個隸書字通常只有一個燕尾。看看「三」：只有最下面那條長橫有燕尾，上面兩條的收筆都是圓的。後來的書法家把這個習慣說成一句口訣：「雁不雙飛，蠶不二設」（燕尾也叫雁尾）。
隸書是漢代通行的字體。人們用毛筆把字寫在窄窄的竹片和木片上，再用繩子編成一冊。1930 到 1931 年，西北邊疆的居延附近出土了一萬多枚漢代的簡，現在收藏在台北的中央研究院。
這一課，在 3D 裡分三段重播長橫，看小篆變成隸書，再攤開一卷竹簡。接著拖動兩種字體之間的那條線、找出燕尾，再自己描寫看看。
questions: According to Xu Shen, why did clerical script appear in the Qin dynasty?
How does the brush make a silkworm head and a swallow tail?
In the clerical character 三, which line has the swallow tail?
answers: The government offices and prisons had so much work that people needed a way to write that was quick and simple.
For the head, the brush touches down moving backward, then turns and goes right. For the tail, it presses down, then lifts as it flicks up to the right.
Only the long bottom line. The two lines above end round.

quiz.q: In which dynasty did clerical script begin?
Which way does the brush move first to make a silkworm head?
How many swallow tails does a clerical character usually have?
options: As many as it has lines

quiz.q: What did people in the Han dynasty often write on?
What happened to the tall shapes of seal script in clerical script?

parts.text_en: One line that has everything: a silkworm head at the start and a swallow tail at the end. In seal script it is just an even line.
parts.text_zh: 一條線就有全部：起筆是蠶頭，收筆是燕尾。它的小篆只是一條粗細一樣的線。

parts.text_en: Three lines, but only the long bottom line gets the swallow tail. The two short lines end round. In seal script, all three lines are the same length.
parts.text_zh: 三條橫線，只有最下面那條長的有燕尾，上面兩條短的收筆是圓的。它的小篆三條線一樣長。

parts.text_en: Two horizontals and a vertical. The tail belongs to the long bottom line, and the tall seal-script shape has become low and wide.
parts.text_zh: 兩橫一豎，燕尾在最下面那條長橫；小篆高高的字形，變得又矮又寬。

parts.text_en: The curved base of the seal form, shaped like a bowl, has become a straight line with a square corner, and it ends in the tail.
parts.text_zh: 小篆像碗一樣彎彎的底，變成一條直線和一個方方的轉角，最後帶出燕尾。

parts.text_en: With no long horizontal, the right-falling stroke carries the tail. The curving seal form has become two plain strokes.
parts.text_zh: 沒有長橫的字，燕尾就在捺上。小篆彎彎的線條，變成簡單的兩筆。

parts.text_en: The five curving lines of the seal form have become four strokes of straight lines and turns. The last, right-falling stroke carries the tail.
parts.text_zh: 小篆的五條彎線，變成四筆直線和轉折；最後一筆捺帶著燕尾。

lessons.parts_note_en: The red stroke in each picture is the one with the swallow tail. Tap Watch it in 3D to see the brush write the character over its seal-script form.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 每張小圖裡紅色的那一筆，就是有燕尾的那一筆。點「在模型中看」，看毛筆在小篆上面寫出這個字。

wipe.eyebrow: Before and After · 前後對照
wipe.en: Drag the line: seal script to clerical script
wipe.zh: 拖動分隔線：從小篆到隸書
wipe.lead_en: Left of the gold line is small seal script; right of it is clerical script. Drag the line, or move the slider, to compare the same character before and after the change.
wipe.lead_zh: 金色的線左邊是小篆，右邊是隸書。拖動那條線（或拉滑桿），比一比同一個字變化前後的樣子。

yi.en: Seal script: one even line with round ends. Clerical script: the same line, now with a head at the start and a tail at the end.
yi.zh: 小篆：一條粗細一樣、兩頭圓圓的線。隸書：同一條線，起筆多了蠶頭、收筆多了燕尾。

san.en: Seal script: three even lines of the same length, standing tall. Clerical script: the lines move closer together, the bottom one grows longest, and only it has a tail.
san.zh: 小篆：三條一樣長的線，排得高高的。隸書：三條線靠近了，最下面那條最長，也只有它有燕尾。

tu.en: Seal script: a tall vertical line with two even lines across it. Clerical script: the vertical is shorter, the base is wider, and the base ends in a tail.
tu.zh: 小篆：一條長長的豎線，加上兩條橫線。隸書：豎變短、底變寬，底下那一橫帶著燕尾。

shan.en: Seal script: three tall lines standing in a curved base. Clerical script: the curve becomes a straight base with a square corner.
shan.zh: 小篆：三條長線站在彎彎的底上。隸書：彎彎的底變成直線，轉彎的地方變成方角。

ren.en: Seal script: long curving lines. Clerical script: a left-falling stroke and a right-falling stroke with a tail.
ren.zh: 小篆：長長的彎線。隸書：一撇，加上一筆帶著燕尾的捺。

shui.en: Seal script: five curving lines, like running water. Clerical script: straight lines and turns, wider than it is tall.
shui.zh: 小篆：五條彎彎的線，像流動的水。隸書：變成直線和轉折，字形寬比高大。

tail.lead_en: Each clerical character here has exactly one swallow tail. Tap the stroke that has it.
tail.lead_zh: 這裡每個隸書字都正好有一個燕尾。點一下有燕尾的那一筆。

pad.lead_en: Choose a character and trace it. On the pad, slow means thick and fast means thin: slow down for the head, slow down again to press before the tail, then speed up as you flick up to the right.
pad.lead_zh: 選一個字描寫看看。在練字板上，慢就粗、快就細：寫蠶頭時慢一點，燕尾前再慢下來「按」一下，往右上挑出去的時候加快。

tips.en: For the head, start a little to the right, move left, then turn and go right.
tips.zh: 寫蠶頭：從右邊一點的地方下筆，先往左，再回頭往右走。

tips.en: For the tail, press, then flick up to the right and lift.
tips.zh: 寫燕尾：先按，再往右上挑、提起來。

tips.en: In 三, only the bottom line gets a tail.
tips.zh: 寫「三」：只有最下面那一橫有燕尾。

links_head.eyebrow: Before and Next · 上一課與下一課
links_head.en: From seal script to regular script

links.en: Where Did Chinese Characters Come From?
links.zh: 漢字從哪裡來？甲骨文到篆書
links.note_en: Oracle bone script, bronze script, and small seal script: the forms that came before clerical script.
links.note_zh: 甲骨文、金文、小篆：隸書之前的字體。

links.en: Regular, Running, Cursive: How Fast Can You Write?
links.zh: 楷書、行書、草書：同一個字，三種速度
links.note_en: Regular script grew out of clerical script and dropped the flicked tail. Then writers went faster: strokes joined in running script and flew in cursive script.
links.note_zh: 楷書由隸書演變而來，少了往上挑的尾巴。接著越寫越快：行書把筆畫連起來，草書寫得像在飛。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories of Clerical Script · 隸書的故事
culture_cards.title_en: Busy offices, slips from a tomb, slips from the frontier, and a famous stone
culture_cards.title_zh: 忙碌的官府、秦墓裡的竹簡、邊疆的木簡，和一塊有名的石碑
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about where clerical script came from and where we can still see it.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於隸書從哪裡來、今天在哪裡還看得到的四個小故事。

cards.en: Too much work, not enough time
cards.body_en: Xu Shen wrote that in the Qin dynasty the offices and prisons had so much work that clerical script appeared, to make writing quick and simple. A later history, the Book of Jin, says that seal script was hard to finish, so lowly clerks were told to help with the writing, and the script was named after them. It adds that clerical script is the quick form of seal script.
cards.body_zh: 許慎說，秦代「官獄職務繁，初有隸書，以趣約易」：官府和監獄的事情太多，才有了寫起來又快又簡單的隸書。《晉書》說，篆字難成，於是「令隸人佐書，曰隸字」——讓地位低的小吏幫忙抄寫，所以叫隸書；又說「隸書者，篆之捷也」，隸書就是寫得快的篆書。

cards.k: Older Than the Story · 更早的隸書
cards.body_en: A famous story says a prisoner named Cheng Miao invented clerical script for the First Emperor. But even the old histories begin that story with “some say.” In 1975, 1,155 bamboo slips were found in a Qin tomb at Shuihudi in Yunmeng, Hubei. They were written by Qin people around the time China was united, in an early clerical script that still looks a little like seal script. Clerical script grew little by little.
cards.body_zh: 有個有名的故事說，囚犯程邈為秦始皇創造了隸書；不過連古代的史書講這個故事時，都先說「或曰」（有人說）。1975 年，湖北雲夢睡虎地的秦墓出土了 1,155 枚竹簡，是秦統一六國前後秦人的墨跡，用早期的隸書（秦隸）書寫，結構還帶著篆書的樣子。可見隸書是一點一點慢慢形成的。

cards.en: Slips from the frontier, kept in Taipei
cards.body_en: In 1930 and 1931, an expedition found more than 10,000 Han dynasty slips near Juyan, on the northwest frontier: soldiers' reports, lists, and writing practice, most of them in clerical script. During the war years they were moved to Hong Kong and then to the Library of Congress in the United States, and in November 1965 they arrived in Taiwan. Academia Sinica's museum in Taipei shows more than 200 of them, including a national treasure: a book of 77 wooden slips from the years 93 to 95, still tied together with its cords.
cards.body_zh: 1930 到 1931 年，西北科學考察團在西北邊疆的居延附近發現一萬多枚漢代的簡：士兵的報告、名冊和練字的簡，大量使用隸書。戰爭期間，這批簡先運到香港，再運到美國國會圖書館保存，1965 年 11 月運抵台灣。位在台北的中央研究院歷史文物陳列館展出其中兩百多支，包括一件國寶：東漢永元五年到七年（西元 93–95 年）的一份簡冊，77 支木簡還用編繩連在一起。

cards.k: A Model for Learners · 範本
cards.body_en: The Cao Quan Stele is a stone tablet carved in clerical script in the year 185, in the Eastern Han dynasty. It was dug up many centuries later, in the Wanli years of the Ming dynasty, and now stands in the Forest of Steles in Xi'an. The Ministry of Education's dictionary calls its writing graceful and strong, and many people who learn clerical script use it as their model. The National Palace Museum in Taipei has an ink rubbing of it.
cards.body_zh: 曹全碑是東漢中平二年（西元 185 年）的隸書碑刻，到明朝萬曆年間才出土，現在存放在西安碑林。教育部辭典說它「書法秀麗而有骨力，學習隸書者，多用為範本」。台北的國立故宮博物院藏有它的墨拓本。

myths.myth_en: Clerical script is older than seal script.
myths.myth_zh: 隸書比篆書古老。
myths.fact_en: It is the other way around. Clerical script is a simpler form of seal script. It began in the Qin dynasty and was common in the Han and Wei dynasties.
myths.fact_zh: 正好相反。隸書是篆書的簡化體，創始於秦，通行於漢、魏。

myths.myth_en: Every horizontal line in clerical script has a swallow tail.
myths.myth_zh: 隸書的每一條橫線都有燕尾。
myths.fact_en: Usually only one stroke in a character has it. In 三, the two short lines end round, and only the bottom line flicks up.
myths.fact_zh: 通常一個字只有一筆有燕尾。「三」上面兩條短橫收筆是圓的，只有最下面那條往上挑。

myths.myth_en: To make a silkworm head, you draw a little circle.
myths.myth_zh: 蠶頭是畫一個小圓圈畫出來的。
myths.fact_en: The brush does not draw a circle. It touches down moving backward, then turns and goes right. The turn is hidden inside the stroke, and that makes the start look round.
myths.fact_zh: 毛筆不是畫圓圈，而是先逆著入紙、再回頭往右走。回鋒藏在筆畫裡面，起筆才看起來圓圓的。

myths.myth_en: One man invented clerical script in prison.
myths.myth_zh: 隸書是一個人在監獄裡發明的。
myths.fact_en: That is the old story about Cheng Miao, and even old histories tell it with “some say.” Bamboo slips found at Shuihudi in 1975 show an early clerical script already in use around the time China was united. It grew over many years, in many hands.
myths.fact_zh: 那是關於程邈的老故事，連古代史書都用「或曰」來講。1975 年睡虎地出土的竹簡顯示，秦統一前後就有人用早期的隸書寫字了。隸書是很多人、很多年慢慢寫出來的。

tricks.body_en: Start with a round head; end with a flick up to the right.
tricks.body_zh: 起筆圓圓的，收筆往右上挑。

tricks.body_en: The brush goes in backward, then turns.
tricks.body_zh: 筆尖逆著入紙，再回頭往右走。

tricks.body_en: Wild geese do not fly in pairs: one flicked tail is enough.
tricks.body_zh: 一個字只放一個燕尾（雁尾）。

tricks.title_en: Seal is tall, clerical is flat
tricks.body_en: Round turns become square corners.
tricks.body_zh: 圓轉變成方折。

safety.en: Ink stains clothes and is very hard to wash out. Wear old clothes or an apron, and roll up your sleeves.
safety.zh: 墨沾到衣服很難洗掉：穿舊衣服或圍裙，袖子捲起來。

safety.en: Cover the desk with old newspaper, and keep the ink in a heavy, steady dish so it will not tip over.
safety.zh: 桌上先鋪舊報紙；墨要裝在重一點、放得穩的碟子裡，免得打翻。

safety.en: Press gently. Crushing the brush against the paper squashes the hairs and can split or break them.
safety.zh: 輕輕地按就好：把筆用力壓在紙上，筆毛會擠扁，也可能分岔或折斷。

safety.en: Do not put the brush, the ink, or the ink stick in your mouth, and do not lick the brush tip to shape it.
safety.zh: 毛筆、墨汁、墨條都不要放進嘴裡，也不要用嘴巴舔筆尖。

safety.en: After writing, wash the brush in clean water until the water runs clear, gently shape it into a point, and hang it tip-down or lay it flat to dry. Wash your hands, too.
safety.zh: 寫完後用清水洗筆，洗到水變清為止；輕輕把筆毛理成尖形，筆尖朝下掛起來或平放晾乾。也要洗手。

materials.en: A brush and a cup of clean water for each student
materials.zh: 每人一枝毛筆、一杯清水

materials.en: Old newspaper, or a small blackboard
materials.zh: 舊報紙，或一塊小黑板

steps.en: Say the five moves out loud: left, turn, go, press, flick.
steps.zh: 先大聲唸五個動作：往左、回頭、走、按、挑。

steps.en: Write a long horizontal line with water, saying each move as you do it.
steps.zh: 用清水寫一條長橫，邊寫邊唸每一個動作。

steps.en: Look quickly before the water dries: is the head round? Does the tail point up to the right?
steps.zh: 趁水還沒乾趕快看：頭是圓的嗎？尾巴有沒有往右上翹？

steps.en: Now write 三. Remember: only the bottom line gets a tail.
steps.zh: 接著寫「三」。記得：只有最下面那一橫有燕尾。

activities.tip_en: Water costs nothing and leaves no stain, so students can try the same stroke twenty times.
activities.tip_zh: 清水不用錢、也不會弄髒，同一筆可以練二十次。

materials.en: Eight to ten craft sticks, or strips of thick paper, for each student
materials.zh: 每人八到十根冰棒棍，或一樣大小的厚紙條

materials.en: Two pieces of string, each about as long as your arm
materials.zh: 兩條繩子，每條大約一隻手臂長

materials.en: A marker or a small brush
materials.zh: 一枝麥克筆或小毛筆

steps.en: Lay the sticks side by side. Tie them together with the two strings, one near the top and one near the bottom, weaving over and under.
steps.zh: 把冰棒棍一根根並排，用兩條繩子一上一下穿過去綁好：一條靠近上面，一條靠近下面。

steps.en: Write one character on each stick from top to bottom, starting with the stick on the right.
steps.zh: 從最右邊那一根開始，在每一根上由上往下寫字。

steps.en: Roll up your scroll, then unroll it and read it to a classmate.
steps.zh: 把竹簡捲起來，再攤開唸給同學聽。

steps.en: Look at the character 冊. Can you see the slips and the two cords?
steps.zh: 看看「冊」這個字：看得出竹片和兩道繩子嗎？

activities.tip_en: Writing from the right-hand stick first follows the old way of reading: top to bottom, right to left.
activities.tip_zh: 從最右邊那一根寫起，是照古書的讀法：由上到下、由右到左。

sources.en: Clerical script: a simpler form of seal script, begun in the Qin and common in the Han and Wei; the horizontal stroke starts like a silkworm's head and ends like a wild goose's tail
sources.zh: 隸書：篆書的簡化體，創始於秦，通行於漢、魏；橫畫起筆回鋒如蠶頭，收筆頓筆挑起如雁尾
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「隸書」

sources.en: 蠶頭雁尾: the start turns back and swells like a silkworm's head; the end presses and flicks up like a wild goose's tail
sources.zh: 蠶頭雁尾：橫畫起筆回鋒，隆起如蠶頭之形；收筆頓筆挑起，具雁尾之狀
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「蠶頭雁尾」

sources.en: Libian: the process of rewriting seal script as clerical script
sources.zh: 隸變：文字學上指篆書改寫成隸書的經過
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「隸變」

sources.en: Shuowen postface: in the Qin, office and prison work was heavy, so clerical script first appeared, to be quick and simple
sources.zh: 《說文解字．敘》：「官獄職務繁，初有隸書，以趣約易」
sources.src: 維基文庫《說文解字》卷十五

sources.en: Cheng Miao: a jailer imprisoned at Yunyang who simplified small seal script; the First Emperor pardoned him and named the writing clerical script
sources.zh: 程邈：嘗為縣獄吏，因獲罪幽繫於雲陽，在獄中省改小篆，創新體，始皇善之而赦其罪，名其書為隸書
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「程邈」

sources.en: Regular script: grew out of clerical script; the main difference is leaving out the flick at the end
sources.zh: 楷書：由隸書演變而來，與隸書的主要區別為省略尾部的挑筆
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「楷書」

sources.en: Book of Jin, biography of Wei Heng: seal script was hard to finish, so clerks (隸人) were told to help write; “clerical script is the quick form of seal script”; the Cheng Miao story introduced with “some say” (或曰)
sources.zh: 《晉書．衛恆傳》：「篆字難成，即令隸人佐書，曰隸字」「隸書者，篆之捷也」；程邈的故事以「或曰」帶出
sources.src: 維基文庫《晉書》卷三十六

sources.en: Shuihudi Qin slips: bamboo slips unearthed in 1975 at Yunmeng, Hubei; written by Qin people around the unification, in Qin clerical script that still keeps the feel of seal script
sources.zh: 睡虎地秦簡：民國六十四年於湖北省雲夢出土的竹簡，約為秦始皇統一六國前後之秦人墨跡，用秦隸書寫，稍具波磔，結構仍存篆意
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「睡虎地秦簡」

sources.en: Shuihudi: found in December 1975 in tomb no. 11; 1,155 slips after sorting (interview with the Hubei Provincial Museum, June 24, 2024)
sources.zh: 睡虎地 11 號墓 1975 年 12 月出土，經整理共 1,155 枚（湖北省博物館受訪，2024 年 6 月 24 日）
sources.src: 中國新聞社（2024）

sources.en: The saying 雁不雙飛，蠶不二設 (a later teaching formula; found in a 19th-century text)
sources.zh: 「蚕頭鴈尾。鴈不雙飛。蚕不二設。」（後人的口訣；見十九世紀朝鮮李裕元〈書家正派說〉）
sources.src: 維基文庫《嘉梧藁略》冊十一

sources.en: Han slips: the largest group was found by the Northwest Scientific Expedition near Juyan in 1930 (Juyan Han slips)
sources.zh: 漢簡：以西北科學考察團於民國十九年在居延附近所發現者為最多，稱為「居延漢簡」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「漢簡」

sources.en: Juyan Han slips: more than 200 slips on display; Juyan was on the northwest frontier of the Han, guarded by soldiers; items include reports, registers, practice slips, cords, and a brush
sources.zh: 居延漢簡：展出 200 餘支；居延位於漢代的西北邊境，派兵屯田戍衛；展品有報告、名籍、習字簡、繩、毛筆
sources.src: 中研院史語所歷史文物陳列館〈居延漢簡〉

sources.en: Juyan Han slips: excavated in 1930–1931 by Folke Bergman and others; more than 11,000 pieces; records of soldiers and residents from the mid Western Han to the early Eastern Han
sources.zh: 居延漢簡：1930–1931 年貝格曼等人發掘，約 11,000 餘枚；西漢中晚期到東漢初期當地軍民的紀錄
sources.src: 中研院史語所「漢代簡牘數位典藏」說明

sources.en: The slips' journey: Hong Kong after 1937, shipped to the United States in August 1940 and kept at the Library of Congress, arrived in Taiwan on November 23, 1965 (Kao Chen-huan, 2024)
sources.zh: 漢簡的旅程：1937 年後到香港，1940 年 8 月運往美國國會圖書館，1965 年 11 月 23 日抵達臺灣（高震寰，2024）
sources.src: 中研院史語所九十五週年文集

sources.en: Juyan slips use clerical script in great numbers, with some cursive and a little seal script
sources.zh: 居延出土的簡牘除了大量使用隸書，也用草書和少量篆書
sources.src: 中研院史語所歷史文物陳列館（2012–2015 展覽）

sources.en: A national treasure: the most complete Han slip book found so far, 77 slips joined by cords, dated 93–95 CE
sources.zh: 國寶〈廣地南部永元五年至七年官兵釜磑月言及四時簿〉：迄今保存最完整的漢代簡冊，編繩編連七十七支簡，西元 93–95 年
sources.src: 中研院史語所歷史文物陳列館

sources.en: Frontier slips were mostly poplar, tamarisk, and pine, with a little bamboo; single slips were bound into scrolls to hold longer writing
sources.zh: 邊塞漢簡的主要原料是胡楊木、紅柳和松木等，還有少數的竹；編聯成簡冊可以書寫更完整的內容
sources.src: 中研院史語所歷史文物陳列館〈從原料、編寫到再利用──邊塞漢簡的生命史〉（2023 年起展出）

sources.en: Bamboo slips: before paper was invented, bamboo was cut into slips to write on; “自古書契多編以竹簡” (Hou Hanshu)
sources.zh: 竹簡：古代紙未發明前，將竹剖削成片，在上面刻寫文字；《後漢書．蔡倫傳》：「自古書契多編以竹簡」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「竹簡」

sources.en: Shuowen on 冊: slips of different lengths with two cords through them
sources.zh: 《說文解字》「冊」：象其札一長一短，中有二編之形
sources.src: 維基文庫《說文解字》卷二

sources.en: Cao Quan Stele: a Han clerical-script stele, unearthed in the Wanli era of the Ming; often used as a model by learners
sources.zh: 曹全碑：漢朝隸書的碑刻，明萬曆年間始出土；書法秀麗而有骨力，學習隸書者多用為範本
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「曹全碑」

sources.en: Cao Quan Stele: Eastern Han, 185 CE (second year of Zhongping); unearthed in the Wanli era; now in the Forest of Steles, Xi'an

lessons.title: Regular, Running, Cursive: How Fast Can You Write?
lessons.title_zh: 楷書、行書、草書：同一個字，三種速度
lessons.blurb_en: One character, three ways to write it. In regular script every stroke stands alone. In running script the strokes join. In cursive script they melt into one flowing line. Watch three brushes race in 3D, name five scripts in a game, and time your own writing on the practice pad.
lessons.blurb_zh: 同一個字，三種寫法：楷書一筆一畫分開，行書把筆畫連起來，草書連成一條流動的線。看三枝毛筆在 3D 裡比賽，玩五種字體的認字遊戲，再用練字板的碼表量量自己寫多快。
lessons.big_idea_en: Regular, running, and cursive script are three ways to write the same character. Regular script writes each stroke separately, so it is the clearest and the slowest. Running script links the strokes, so it is quicker and still easy to read. Cursive script joins and simplifies the strokes, so it is the fastest and the hardest to read.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 楷書、行書、草書，是同一個字的三種寫法。楷書一筆一畫分開寫，最清楚、也最慢；行書把筆畫連起來，比較快、還認得出來；草書把筆畫連在一起又簡化，最快、也最難認。

lab.how_en: Drag to turn, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Three brushes write the same character at the same time: regular script on the left, running script in the middle, and cursive script on the right. Watch the timers, then choose one script to look closer, or change the character.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。三枝毛筆同時寫同一個字：左邊楷書、中間行書、右邊草書。看看每張紙上的計時，再選一種字體近看，或換一個字。

legend.en: Bright label: the script that finishes first
legend.zh: 亮起來的標籤：最先寫完的字體

legend.en: Thread: a thin line where the brush does not quite leave the paper
legend.zh: 牽絲：筆沒有完全離開紙的細線

legend.en: Red lines: the 米 grid, 21 centimeters wide
legend.zh: 紅線：米字格，寬 21 公分

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. The times are calculated by our model, not measured from a real calligrapher: the brush takes time for the careful start and finish of every stroke, and each lift between strokes costs 0.82 seconds. The running and cursive forms are our own tracings over an early copy of the Lanting Xu and a rubbing of Zhiyong's Thousand Character Classic.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型。時間是模型算出來的，不是量真人寫字：每一筆仔細的起筆和收筆都要花時間，筆和筆之間每提筆一次算 0.82 秒。行書和草書的字形，是我們對著〈蘭亭序〉的古摹本和智永〈真草千字文〉的拓本自己描的。
lab.credit_html: Model, stroke data, and the writing engine are drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect. Running-script reference: the Shenlong copy of the Lanting Xu (Wikimedia Commons, public domain). Cursive-script reference: 墨拓智永書真草千文 冊, The National Palace Museum, Taipei, CC BY 4.0 @ www.npm.gov.tw. · 模型、筆畫資料與寫字引擎由人師教育協會自繪、自寫；行書對位參考神龍本〈蘭亭序〉（維基共享資源，公有領域），草書對位參考國立故宮博物院〈墨拓智永書真草千文 冊〉（CC BY 4.0）。

paras: Write your name slowly and neatly. Now write it again as fast as you can. The letters lean, join, and lose some of their parts. Chinese calligraphy has names for these different ways of writing. Three of them are regular script, running script, and cursive script.

In regular script, every stroke is written separately. The brush starts each stroke with care, finishes it with care, and then leaves the paper before the next one. This makes regular script the clearest of the three, and the slowest. It is the form you see in textbooks and learn first.

Running script sits between regular and cursive script. The Ministry of Education's dictionary says it is close to regular script but more flowing and lively. The brush does not always leave the paper, so some strokes are joined by a thin line called a thread. The characters are quicker to write and still easy to recognize.

Cursive script was made for speed. The same dictionary says it appeared so that people could write conveniently and quickly. Strokes are joined, shortened, or left out, so a whole character can become one or two flowing lines. It is the fastest of the three, and the hardest to read.

Here is a surprise: cursive script is not regular script written in a hurry. It began around the Qin and Han dynasties as a quick way to write clerical script. Regular script took shape later, in the Later Han dynasty, and was complete by the Wei. So the three scripts are three ways of writing, and all three are still used today.

In this lesson, three brushes write the same character at the same time, and you can see which one finishes first. Then name all five scripts you have met in this unit, and use the stopwatch on the practice pad to find your own three speeds.
paras_zh: 慢慢地、整整齊齊地寫下你的名字；再用最快的速度寫一次。字母歪了、連在一起了，有些地方還不見了。中文書法替這些不同的寫法取了名字，其中三種是：楷書、行書、草書。
楷書一筆一畫分開寫。每一筆都仔細地起筆、仔細地收筆，筆離開紙以後，才寫下一筆。所以楷書是三種裡面最清楚、也最慢的。課本上印的、你最先學的，就是這種字。
行書介於楷書和草書之間。教育部辭典說，它接近楷書，但筆勢比較流暢活潑。毛筆不一定每次都離開紙，有些筆畫之間就留下一條細細的線，叫做「牽絲」。行書寫起來比較快，也還很容易認。
草書是為了快而產生的。同一本辭典說，它是「為書寫方便、快速而產生的字體」。筆畫有的連起來、有的縮短、有的省略，一個字可能變成一兩條流動的線。它是三種裡面最快、也最難認的。
有件事可能讓你意外：草書不是把楷書寫快變來的。草書大約在秦漢之際就出現了，一開始是隸書的快寫；楷書比較晚才成形，大約起源於後漢，到魏才完備。所以這三種字體是三種寫法，而且到今天都還有人在寫。
這一課，三枝毛筆同時寫同一個字，看看哪一枝最先寫完；再認一認這個單元學過的五種字體，然後用練字板的碼表，量量你自己的三種速度。
questions: Which of the three scripts is the clearest, and which is the fastest?
What is a thread in running script?
Did cursive script come from writing regular script quickly? What does the lesson say?
answers: Regular script is the clearest. Cursive script is the fastest.
It is a thin line that joins two strokes, left where the brush does not quite leave the paper.
No. Cursive script began around the Qin and Han dynasties as a quick way to write clerical script. Regular script took shape later.

vocab.exzh: 用一條直線把兩個點連起來。

vocab.ex: The skater made one smooth turn after another.
vocab.exzh: 溜冰的人做出一個又一個流暢的轉彎。

vocab.ex: The train picked up speed as it left the station.

parts.text_en: Five strokes, and every one has its own careful start and finish. Between strokes, the brush leaves the paper four times.
parts.text_zh: 五筆，每一筆都有自己的起筆和收筆。筆和筆之間，毛筆離開紙四次。

parts.text_en: Four strokes: the left-falling stroke runs straight into the right-falling stroke. The red lines are threads, where the brush hardly leaves the paper. Traced from an early copy of the Lanting Xu.
parts.text_zh: 四筆：撇直接連到捺。紅色的細線是牽絲，毛筆在那裡幾乎沒有離開紙。字形描自〈蘭亭序〉的古摹本（神龍本）。

parts.meta_zh: 1 筆・提筆 0 次・8.5 秒
parts.text_en: One line. The dot, the hook, and both sides are joined and simplified into a single looping stroke. Traced from a rubbing of Zhiyong's Thousand Character Classic.
parts.text_zh: 一筆到底。點、鉤和左右兩邊連在一起、又簡化了，變成一條繞圈的線。字形描自智永〈真草千字文〉的拓本。

lessons.parts_note_en: The numbers come from our model of the character 永. Tap Watch it in 3D to see each script written by itself.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 卡片上的數字是用我們的模型算「永」字得到的。點「在模型中看」，單獨看每一種字體怎麼寫。

sheets.eyebrow: From the Masters · 法帖裡的字
sheets.en: What the real ones look like
sheets.lead_en: Our running and cursive characters are tracings. Here are the works we traced them from.
sheets.lead_zh: 模型裡的行書和草書是我們描的。這裡是我們照著描的法帖。

items.alt_en: A rubbing with the character 永 in regular script on the right and cursive script on the left
items.alt_zh: 拓本：右邊楷書的「永」，左邊草書的「永」
items.en: 永 in regular and cursive script
items.text_en: Zhiyong, a monk and a descendant of Wang Xizhi, wrote the Thousand Character Classic in regular and cursive script side by side, which helps learners recognize the cursive forms. Here the regular 永 is on the right and the cursive 永 on the left. This rubbing was made from a stone carved in 1109.
items.text_zh: 智永是王羲之的後代，也是一位出家人。他把〈千字文〉用楷書和草書並排寫出來，方便學的人認草書。圖中右邊是楷書的「永」，左邊是草書的「永」。這份拓本拓自大觀三年（1109）刻的石碑。
items.credit_html: 墨拓智永書真草千文 冊, The National Palace Museum, Taipei, CC BY 4.0 @ www.npm.gov.tw

items.alt_en: A rubbing with the character 水 in regular script on the right and cursive script on the left
items.alt_zh: 拓本：右邊楷書的「水」，左邊草書的「水」
items.en: 水 in regular and cursive script
items.text_en: From the same rubbing: the regular 水 on the right has four strokes. In the cursive 水 on the left, they have become three short curves.
items.text_zh: 同一份拓本：右邊楷書的「水」有四筆；左邊草書的「水」，變成三條短短的彎線。

items.alt_en: The opening characters 永和九年 of the Lanting Xu in running script
items.alt_zh: 〈蘭亭序〉開頭「永和九年」四個行書字
items.en: 永和九年 in running script
items.text_en: The first four characters of the Lanting Xu: 永和九年, the ninth year of Yonghe (353). Wang Xizhi's original is lost. This is from an early tracing copy known as the Shenlong copy. Our running-script 永 was traced from the first character.
items.text_zh: 〈蘭亭序〉開頭四個字「永和九年」（353）。王羲之的原蹟已經失傳，這是一件古摹本（神龍本）。我們行書的「永」，就是照著第一個字描的。

scripts.lead_en: You have now met five scripts: seal, clerical, regular, running, and cursive. Look at each character and name its script. Ten questions make a round.
scripts.lead_zh: 到這一課，你已經認識五種字體：篆書、隸書、楷書、行書、草書。看看每個字，說出它是哪一種字體。一輪十題。

seal.en: Seal script has smooth lines of the same width, with rounded turns.
seal.zh: 篆書的線條圓滑、粗細一樣，轉彎是圓的。

clerical.en: Clerical script is flat and wide, and one stroke ends in a flicked tail.
clerical.zh: 隸書字形扁扁寬寬，有一筆的收筆往上挑。

regular.en: Regular script has separate strokes, each with a clear start and finish.
regular.zh: 楷書一筆一畫分開，起筆、收筆都很清楚。

running.en: Running script joins some strokes, but you can still see every part.
running.zh: 行書把一些筆畫連起來，但每個部分都還看得出來。

cursive.en: Cursive script joins and simplifies the strokes into a few flowing lines.
cursive.zh: 草書把筆畫連在一起又簡化，變成幾條流動的線。

pad.lead_en: Choose a script and a character, then trace it. The stopwatch runs from your first touch to your last lift, and it counts how many times you lift.
pad.lead_zh: 選一種字體、一個字，描寫看看。碼表從你第一筆下筆算到最後一筆提筆，也會數你提筆幾次。

tips.en: Trace the regular form first, stroke by stroke. Then try the running form without stopping at the thin threads.
tips.zh: 先一筆一筆描楷書，再描行書：遇到細細的牽絲不要停。

tips.en: For the cursive form, tap Watch the demo first. Follow the line the way the brush goes.
tips.zh: 描草書以前先按「看示範」，照著毛筆走的方向寫。

tips.en: Compare your three times. Which script was the fastest for you?
tips.zh: 比一比你的三個時間：哪一種字體你寫得最快？

links.zh: 隸書：為什麼是蠶頭燕尾？
