culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories of Three Scripts · 三種字體的故事
culture_cards.title_en: Stand, walk, run; a monk's model book; the most famous running script; and cursive treasures in Taipei
culture_cards.title_zh: 站、走、跑；智永的範本；最有名的行書；台北故宮的草書國寶
culture_cards.lead_en: Four short stories about writing slowly, writing quickly, and learning to do both.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 關於慢慢寫、快快寫，還有兩種都要學的四個小故事。

cards.body_en: The Song dynasty writer Su Shi put it this way: regular script is like standing, running script is like walking, and cursive script is like running, and nobody can run before learning to stand and walk. (English says running script, but 行 means to walk.) In Taiwan, elementary school students practice regular script, and in junior high they learn to recognize the different scripts.
cards.body_zh: 宋代的蘇軾說：「真如立，行如行，草如走，未有未能行立而能走者也。」楷書像站著，行書像走路，草書像跑步（古文的「走」是跑）；還不會站、不會走的人，不可能會跑。在台灣，國小學生練寫楷書，到國中「認識各種書體」。

cards.body_en: Zhiyong was a monk and a seventh-generation descendant of Wang Xizhi. He is said to have written 800 copies of the Thousand Character Classic, each in regular and cursive script, and given them to temples. Putting the two scripts side by side helps learners recognize the cursive forms. The National Palace Museum in Taipei has a rubbing of a version carved in stone in 1109; the pictures above come from it.
cards.body_zh: 智永是一位出家人，也是王羲之的七世孫。據記載，他臨寫了八百本〈真草千字文〉，每一本都用楷書和草書並列，分送給各寺院。兩種字體並排，方便學的人認草書。台北國立故宮博物院藏有大觀三年（1109）刻石的拓本，上面的圖片就是從那裡來的。

cards.en: The best running script under heaven
cards.body_en: In 353, Wang Xizhi and his friends met at the Orchid Pavilion to write poems, and he wrote the preface to their poems: the Lanting Xu. It has long been called the best running script under heaven. The original is lost, and we know it only from copies. Our running-script 永 was traced from the first character of one early tracing copy, known as the Shenlong copy. Lesson 8 tells the story.
cards.body_zh: 東晉永和九年（353），王羲之和謝安等四十一人在蘭亭聚會作詩，他為詩集寫了序，就是〈蘭亭序〉，素有「天下第一行書」之稱。原蹟已經失傳，今天只能看到摹本。我們行書的「永」，就是照著一件古摹本（神龍本）的第一個字描的。第八課會說這個故事。

cards.body_en: Two famous cursive scrolls are in the National Palace Museum in Taipei, and both are National Treasures. Sun Guoting wrote his Treatise on Calligraphy (書譜) in 687. The monk Huaisu wrote his Autobiography (自敘帖) in 777 in wild cursive, the freest kind, with many simplified and joined strokes.
cards.body_zh: 兩件有名的草書長卷都在台北國立故宮博物院，都是國寶。孫過庭的〈書譜〉寫於垂拱三年（687）。出家人懷素的〈自敘帖〉寫於大曆十二年（777），用的是狂草——最奔放的一種草書，簡筆、連筆很多。

myths.myth_en: Cursive script is just messy writing.
myths.myth_zh: 草書就是亂寫。
myths.fact_en: Cursive script has its own forms to learn. Zhiyong wrote a whole model book with every line in regular script and again in cursive, and the Ministry of Education's dictionary calls it an excellent model for learning both.
myths.fact_zh: 草書有自己的寫法要學。智永寫了一整本範本，每一行都有楷書和草書；教育部辭典說它是「學習楷書與草書的絕佳範本」。

myths.myth_en: Cursive script came from writing regular script faster.
myths.myth_zh: 草書是把楷書寫快變來的。
myths.fact_en: It is the other way around in time. Cursive script began around the Qin and Han dynasties as a quick form of clerical script. Regular script took shape in the Later Han and was complete by the Wei.
myths.fact_zh: 時間上正好相反。草書大約起於秦漢之際，是隸書的快寫；楷書約起源於後漢，到魏才完備。

myths.myth_en: In cursive script, the brush never leaves the paper.
myths.myth_zh: 寫草書，毛筆從頭到尾都不離開紙。
myths.fact_en: Sometimes it does. In our tracing of Zhiyong's cursive 水, there are three separate strokes. Early cursive script even kept every character apart from the next one.
myths.fact_zh: 有時候還是會離開。我們描的智永草書「水」就有三筆。早期的草書（章草）甚至每個字都各自獨立，不和下一個字相連。

myths.myth_en: 草書 means “grass writing.”
myths.myth_zh: 「草書」的「草」是青草的草。
myths.fact_en: The character 草 can mean grass, but it also means rough or quick, as in 潦草 (careless writing) and 草稿 (a draft). The dictionary describes early cursive script as clerical script written quickly and roughly.
myths.fact_zh: 「草」可以是青草，但也有「草率、粗略」和「草稿」的意思，像「潦草」「起草」。教育部辭典說，早期的草書是「將隸書草率寫成」。

tricks.body_en: Regular script stands, running script walks, and cursive script runs.
tricks.body_zh: 楷書像站著，行書像走路，草書像跑步。

tricks.body_en: Every stroke starts and finishes by itself.
tricks.body_zh: 每一筆都自己起筆、收筆。

tricks.body_en: A thin line leads the brush to the next stroke.
tricks.body_zh: 細細的線把筆帶到下一筆。

tricks.body_en: Strokes join, shrink, or disappear.
tricks.body_zh: 筆畫連起來、縮短，或省略。

safety.en: Ink stains clothes and is very hard to wash out. Wear old clothes or an apron, and roll up your sleeves.
safety.zh: 墨沾到衣服很難洗掉：穿舊衣服或圍裙，袖子捲起來。

safety.en: Cover the desk with old newspaper, and keep the ink in a heavy, steady dish so it will not tip over.
safety.zh: 桌上先鋪舊報紙；墨要裝在重一點、放得穩的碟子裡，免得打翻。

safety.en: Press gently. Crushing the brush against the paper squashes the hairs and can split or break them.
safety.zh: 輕輕地按就好：把筆用力壓在紙上，筆毛會擠扁，也可能分岔或折斷。

safety.en: Do not put the brush, the ink, or the ink stick in your mouth, and do not lick the brush tip to shape it.
safety.zh: 毛筆、墨汁、墨條都不要放進嘴裡，也不要用嘴巴舔筆尖。

safety.en: After writing, wash the brush in clean water until the water runs clear, gently shape it into a point, and hang it tip-down or lay it flat to dry. Wash your hands, too.
safety.zh: 寫完後用清水洗筆，洗到水變清為止；輕輕把筆毛理成尖形，筆尖朝下掛起來或平放晾乾。也要洗手。

materials.en: A pencil and paper for each student (or a brush and water)
materials.zh: 每人一枝鉛筆和紙（或毛筆和清水）

materials.en: A stopwatch or a phone timer for each pair
materials.zh: 每兩人一個碼表或手機計時器

steps.en: Write 永 slowly, stroke by stroke. Your partner times you and counts how many times your pencil leaves the paper.
steps.zh: 一筆一畫慢慢寫「永」。同伴幫你計時，並數一數鉛筆離開紙幾次。

steps.en: Write it again, lifting the pencil as few times as you can. Time and count again.
steps.zh: 再寫一次，盡量少提筆。再計時、再數一次。

steps.en: Write it a third time as fast as you can. Can your partner still read it?
steps.zh: 第三次用最快的速度寫。同伴還認得出來嗎？

steps.en: Make a small table: lifts and seconds for each try. What changed the most?
steps.zh: 畫一個小表格：每一次提筆幾次、花了幾秒。哪一項變得最多？

activities.tip_en: Ask: when would you choose the slow way? When would the fast way be good enough?
activities.tip_zh: 問問大家：什麼時候要選慢的寫法？什麼時候快的寫法就夠了？

materials.en: This lesson's pictures of Zhiyong's rubbing, shown on a screen or printed
materials.zh: 這一課的智永拓本圖片（投影或印出來）

materials.en: Paper and a pencil
materials.zh: 紙和鉛筆

steps.en: Look at the regular and cursive forms of 永 and 水 side by side. Point to the part of the cursive form that matches each regular stroke.
steps.zh: 把「永」和「水」的楷書、草書放在一起看：指出草書的哪一部分，對應楷書的哪一筆。

steps.en: Which strokes were joined? Which became shorter? Was anything left out?
steps.zh: 哪些筆畫連起來了？哪些變短了？有沒有哪一筆省略了？

steps.en: Now invent a quick form for a simple character, such as 山. Show it to a classmate without saying what it is.
steps.zh: 現在替一個簡單的字（例如「山」）自己設計一個快寫的樣子，不要說是什麼字，拿給同學看。

steps.en: Could they read it? Talk about why cursive script needs forms that everyone learns.
steps.zh: 同學認得出來嗎？討論一下：為什麼草書需要大家都學同一套寫法？

activities.tip_en: This links back to Lesson 4: a shared standard lets people read one another's writing.
activities.tip_zh: 這和第四課有關：有共同的標準，大家才看得懂彼此寫的字。

sources.en: Running script: between regular and cursive script; close to regular script, but more flowing and lively
sources.zh: 行書：筆勢和字形介於楷書與草書之間，近於楷書，但筆勢較流暢活潑
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「行書」

sources.en: Cursive script: made for convenient, quick writing; began around the Qin and Han; early cursive (章草) came from writing clerical script quickly, with separate characters; later cursive joins characters
sources.zh: 草書：為書寫方便、快速而產生的字體，大約起於秦漢之際；章草「將隸書草率寫成…其字個個獨立，不相連綿」；今草筆勢連綴
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「草書」

sources.en: Wild cursive: many simplified and joined strokes, so it is harder to recognize
sources.zh: 狂草：簡筆、連筆甚多，較不易於辨認
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「狂草」

sources.en: Regular script: grew out of clerical script; began in the Later Han, complete by the Wei, still used today
sources.zh: 楷書：由隸書演變而來，約起源於後漢，至魏完備成體，通行至今
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「楷書」

sources.en: Thread (牽絲): in calligraphy, the fine traces left as the brush moves from one stroke to the next
sources.zh: 牽絲：書法上指筆勢往來之間所牽帶的纖細痕跡
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「牽絲」

sources.en: Zhiyong wrote the Thousand Character Classic in regular and cursive script; an excellent model for learning both
sources.zh: 真草千字文：智永以楷書和草書寫成，為學習楷書與草書的絕佳範本
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「真草千字文」

sources.en: Rubbing of Zhiyong's Thousand Character Classic (the Guanzhong version, carved in 1109): regular and cursive side by side to help learners recognize cursive forms; reference for our cursive tracings and source of the two rubbing images
sources.zh: 〈墨拓智永書真草千文 冊〉（關中本，大觀三年 1109 刻）：草、楷並列方便學習者識草認字；草書描線的對位參考與本頁兩張拓本圖片的來源
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院 Open Data（CC BY 4.0）

sources.en: Su Shi: “regular script is like standing, running script like walking, cursive script like running; no one can run before learning to stand and walk”
sources.zh: 蘇軾〈書唐氏六家書後〉：「真生行，行生草，真如立，行如行，草如走，未有未能行立而能走者也。」
sources.src: 維基文庫〈書唐氏六家書後〉

sources.en: Stroke order for the regular-script forms: 永 (5 strokes), 之 (4), 水 (4)
sources.zh: 楷書範字的筆順：「永」5 畫、「之」4 畫、「水」4 畫
sources.src: 教育部《國字標準字體筆順學習網》「之」

sources.en: Lanting Xu: written by Wang Xizhi on the third day of the third month, 353, at a gathering with Xie An, Sun Chuo, and others at the Orchid Pavilion
sources.zh: 蘭亭集序：東晉永和九年（西元 353）三月三日，王羲之與謝安、孫綽等四十一人會於會稽山陰的蘭亭
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「蘭亭集序」

sources.en: The Lanting Xu has long been called the best running script under heaven (天下第一行書)
sources.zh: 〈蘭亭序〉素有「天下第一行書」之稱
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院〈蘭亭癖〉展覽說明

sources.en: The original Lanting Xu is lost
sources.zh: 〈蘭亭序〉原蹟雖已失傳
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院典藏資料檢索〈定武蘭亭真本 卷〉

sources.en: Image of the Shenlong copy of the Lanting Xu (public domain); reference for our running-script tracings and source of the 永和九年 picture
sources.zh: 神龍本〈蘭亭序〉影像（公有領域）：行書描線的對位參考與本頁「永和九年」圖片的來源
sources.src: Wikimedia Commons〈神龍蘭亭序全.JPG〉

sources.en: Zhiyong: said to have written 800 copies of the Thousand Character Classic in regular and cursive script and given them to temples; one ink copy and one carved version (the Guanzhong version) survive
sources.zh: 智永：相傳曾書《真草千字文》八百本，分送浙東諸寺，今尚存墨跡一本，刻本一種（關中本）
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「智永」

sources.en: Sun Guoting's Treatise on Calligraphy (書譜): cursive script, dated 687
sources.zh: 孫過庭〈書譜〉：草書，卷尾題「垂拱三年寫記」（687）
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院精選賞析〈書譜〉

sources.en: Huaisu's Autobiography (自敘帖): wild cursive, dated 777
sources.zh: 懷素〈自敘帖〉：大曆十二年（777）以狂草寫成
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院精選賞析〈自敘帖〉

sources.en: Huaisu's Autobiography: designated a National Treasure on March 26, 2012; regarded as the model of wild cursive
sources.zh: 懷素自敘帖卷：國寶（2012-03-26 指定）；世推為狂草書的代表
sources.src: 文化部文化資產局國家文化資產網

sources.en: Sun Guoting's Treatise on Calligraphy: designated a National Treasure on March 26, 2012
sources.zh: 孫過庭書譜：國寶（2012-03-26 指定）
sources.src: 文化部文化資產局國家文化資產網

sources.en: Taiwan's curriculum: 4-II-7 and 4-III-5, practice regular script (elementary school); 4-IV-4, recognize the different scripts and appreciate famous works (junior high)
sources.zh: 十二年國教國語文領綱：4-Ⅱ-7「掌握楷書筆畫的書寫方法」、4-Ⅲ-5「掌握楷書形體結構的書寫方法」、4-Ⅳ-4「認識各種書體，欣賞名家碑帖」
sources.src: 國家教育研究院《十二年國民基本教育課程綱要：國語文》（2018）

sources.en: Curriculum handbook on 4-IV-4: students learn to tell apart seal, clerical, cursive, regular, and running script
sources.zh: 課程手冊對 4-Ⅳ-4 的說明：讓學生能辨識篆、隸、草、楷、行等各種書體
sources.src: 國家教育研究院《語文領域－國語文課程手冊》（2018）

sources.en: The character 草: also means rough or careless (潦草), a draft (起草), and to write quickly
sources.zh: 「草」：馬虎、粗率（潦草）；底稿、文稿（起草）；草寫
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「草」

sources.en: Early cursive (章草): written quickly from clerical script; the characters are not joined to one another
sources.zh: 章草：一種由隸書草寫而成的字體，各字之間不連屬
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「章草」

units.blurb_en: The Sage of Calligraphy and the Orchid Pavilion, why every master's writing looks different, and the treasures of calligraphy you can see in Taiwan.
units.blurb_zh: 書聖王羲之與蘭亭、為什麼每個書法家的字都不一樣，以及在台灣看得到的書法國寶。

lessons.title: Why Is Wang Xizhi Called the Sage of Calligraphy?
lessons.title_zh: 書聖王羲之：蘭亭序的故事
lessons.blurb_en: One spring day in 353, Wang Xizhi and his friends floated wine cups down a winding stream and wrote poems. Then he wrote a preface that became the most famous piece of running script. Float a cup in 3D, watch the brush write 之 four different ways, and find all twenty in a real copy of the scroll.
lessons.blurb_zh: 西元 353 年的一個春天，王羲之和朋友們在彎彎的小溪上漂酒杯、作詩；他接著寫下一篇序，成了最有名的行書。在 3D 裡放一只酒杯，看毛筆把「之」寫成四種樣子，再到摹本裡找出全部二十個「之」。
lessons.big_idea_en: Wang Xizhi lived in the Eastern Jin dynasty, and later generations called him the Sage of Calligraphy. In 353, at a spring gathering beside a winding stream, he wrote the Lanting Xu, the best-known work of running script. Its 324 characters include 之 twenty times, and no two are written the same way. The original is lost; we know it from later copies.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 王羲之是東晉人，後人稱他「書聖」。永和九年（353）春天，他在一條彎彎的小溪邊和朋友聚會，寫下〈蘭亭序〉——最有名的行書。全文 324 個字裡有二十個「之」，沒有兩個寫得一樣。原蹟已經失傳，我們今天看到的是後來的摹本。

lab.title_en: A Winding Stream and Four Ways to Write 之
lab.title_zh: 曲水流觴，和四個不同的「之」
lab.how_en: Drag to turn, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Float a wine cup down the winding stream and see where it stops. Then choose Four 之 to watch the brush write the same character four different ways, as it appears in a copy of the Lanting Xu.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。在彎彎的小溪上放一只酒杯，看它停在誰面前。再選「四個之」，看毛筆把同一個字寫成四種樣子——都出自〈蘭亭序〉的摹本。

modes.text_en: The guests sit along a winding stream. A cup of wine floats down from upstream, and the guest it stops beside picks it up and drinks. Wang Xizhi wrote: “one cup, one poem.”
modes.text_zh: 客人沿著彎彎的小溪坐下。酒杯從上游漂下來，停在誰面前，誰就拿起來喝。王羲之寫道：「一觴一詠」。

modes.text_en: Four of the twenty 之 from a copy of the Lanting Xu. Each has a dot and a zigzag line, but look how the shapes change: wide, narrow, slanting, tall.
modes.text_zh: 〈蘭亭序〉摹本二十個「之」裡的四個。每一個都是一點加一條彎來彎去的線，可是形狀都不一樣：有的寬、有的窄、有的斜、有的高。

legend.en: Blue ribbon: the winding stream
legend.zh: 藍色的帶子：彎彎的小溪

legend.en: Red cup: a lacquer wine cup with two ears
legend.zh: 紅色的杯子：有兩個耳朵的漆酒杯

legend.en: Yellow label: the guest whose turn it is
legend.zh: 黃色標籤：輪到的那位客人

lab.scale_en: A teaching model, not a picture of the real place: the stream, the pavilion, the bamboo, and the twelve guests are our own simple shapes, and more people came to the real gathering. The cup is a lacquer cup with two ears, a kind used in early China. The four forms of 之 are our own tracings over a copy of the Lanting Xu.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型，不是當年實景：小溪、亭子、竹林和十二位客人都是我們畫的簡單造型，真正參加聚會的人更多。酒杯畫成有兩個耳朵的漆杯（耳杯），是古代常見的一種酒杯。四個「之」是我們對著〈蘭亭序〉摹本自己描的。
lab.credit_html: Model, stroke data, and the writing engine are drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect. The four forms of 之 are our own tracings over the Shenlong copy of the Lanting Xu (Wikimedia Commons (public domain). The scroll is in the Palace Museum, Beijing.) · 模型、筆畫資料與寫字引擎由人師教育協會自繪、自寫；四個「之」對著神龍本〈蘭亭序〉（維基共享資源，公有領域；原卷藏北京故宮博物院）自己描的。

paras: On the third day of the third month in the year 353, Wang Xizhi met his friends at the Orchid Pavilion in Kuaiji, near today's Shaoxing in Zhejiang. It was the day of an old spring custom: people went to the water to wash away bad luck. There were high mountains, tall bamboo, and a clear, fast stream.

The friends sat along a winding stream and played a game. Cups of wine floated down from upstream, and when a cup stopped beside a guest, that guest picked it up and drank. They also wrote poems. An early record says that 26 of them wrote poems that day, and 15 could not and had to drink more wine as a penalty. Wang Xizhi described the day as “one cup, one poem.”

At the end of the day, the poems were gathered into a collection, and Wang Xizhi wrote a preface for it. We call it the Lanting Xu, the Preface to the Orchid Pavilion Collection. It begins with the happy gathering and ends with deeper thoughts about how quickly life passes.

The preface is written in running script. A Tang dynasty writer, He Yanzhi, counted 28 lines and 324 characters. He noticed that when a character appears more than once, each one has a different shape. The character 之 appears most often, about twenty times, and no two are alike. Count them in the gallery below: there are exactly twenty.

Where is the original today? Nobody has it. Tang dynasty books say that Emperor Taizong loved Wang Xizhi's writing so much that the Lanting Xu was buried with him. What we have are copies made by hand in the Tang dynasty and later. That is why museums call the Lanting Xu “the best running script under heaven” and yet can show only copies.

Later generations called Wang Xizhi the Sage of Calligraphy. In this lesson, float a cup down the stream, watch the brush write 之 four different ways, find the matching 之 in the game, and trace them yourself.
paras_zh: 永和九年（353）三月三日，王羲之和朋友們在會稽山陰的蘭亭聚會，地點在今天的浙江紹興。那一天是古老的春天習俗「修禊」：大家到水邊洗濯，去除不祥。那裡有高高的山、長長的竹子，還有一條清澈湍急的溪水。
朋友們沿著彎彎的小溪坐下來，玩一個遊戲：酒杯從上游漂下來，停在誰面前，誰就拿起來喝。大家也作詩。早期的記載說，那天有 26 個人寫出了詩，另外 15 個人寫不出來，被罰喝酒。王羲之形容這一天是「一觴一詠」。
聚會結束後，大家的詩編成一本詩集，王羲之為它寫了一篇序，就是〈蘭亭集序〉，簡稱〈蘭亭序〉。文章從愉快的聚會寫起，最後寫到更深的感想：人生過得好快。
這篇序是用行書寫的。唐朝的何延之數過：一共 28 行、324 個字。他還注意到，同一個字出現不只一次的時候，每一個的寫法都不同；其中「之」字最多，「乃有二十許個，變轉悉異，遂無同者」。到下面的圖裡數數看：正好二十個。
原蹟現在在哪裡？沒有人有。唐朝的書上說，唐太宗非常喜愛王羲之的字，〈蘭亭序〉後來跟著他入葬了。我們今天看到的，是唐朝和後來的人照著摹寫的本子。所以博物館一方面說〈蘭亭序〉是「天下第一行書」，一方面能展出的都是摹本。
後人稱王羲之為「書聖」。這一課，在小溪上放一只酒杯，看毛筆把「之」寫成四種樣子，在遊戲裡找出一樣的「之」，再自己描寫看看。
questions: What game did the friends play beside the stream?
How many times does 之 appear in the Lanting Xu, and what is special about them?
Why can museums show only copies of the Lanting Xu?
answers: They floated cups of wine down a winding stream. When a cup stopped beside a guest, that guest picked it up and drank. They also wrote poems.
Twenty times, and no two are written the same way.
Because the original is lost. Tang dynasty books say it was buried with Emperor Taizong.

vocab.ex: People climbed the mountain to ask the old sage for advice.
vocab.exzh: 人們爬上山，向那位老智者請教。

vocab.ex: Our family has a big gathering every New Year.
vocab.exzh: 我們家每年過年都有一場大聚會。

vocab.ex: We crossed the stream on flat stones.
vocab.exzh: 我們踩著平平的石頭過小溪。

vocab.ex: A leaf floated slowly down the river.
vocab.exzh: 一片葉子慢慢地順著河水漂下去。

vocab.ex: She wrote a short poem about the rain.
vocab.exzh: 她寫了一首關於雨的短詩。

vocab.ex: The author thanks her teacher in the preface.
vocab.exzh: 作者在序裡感謝她的老師。

vocab.ex: This is a print; the original is in a museum.
vocab.exzh: 這是複製畫，原作在博物館裡。

vocab.ex: The dog buried its bone in the garden.
vocab.exzh: 狗把骨頭埋在花園裡。

quiz.q: In which year did Wang Xizhi write the Lanting Xu?
What floated down the winding stream?
Which script is the Lanting Xu written in?
How many times does 之 appear in the Lanting Xu?
What is true about the original Lanting Xu?
options: It is lost; we have only copies.
It was carved on a bone.

parts_head.en: The same character, never the same shape
parts_head.zh: 同一個字，沒有一個長得一樣

parts.text_en: Low and wide. The zigzag slides to the left and ends in a long, heavy line.
parts.text_zh: 又矮又寬。彎線往左滑下去，最後是一條又長又重的橫線。

parts.text_en: The widest of the four, with a sharp turn at the upper right, like the wide world it is describing.
parts.text_zh: 四個裡面最寬的，右上角有一個尖尖的轉折——就像它在寫的「宇宙之大」。

parts.text_en: Small and narrow, written quickly. The last line slants down to the right.
parts.text_zh: 又小又窄，寫得很快。最後一筆往右下斜出去。

parts.text_en: Tall and thin, almost like cursive script. The dot sits high above the line.
parts.text_zh: 又高又瘦，幾乎像草書。上面那一點離得高高的。

lessons.parts_note_en: These four are our own tracings. Tap Watch it in 3D to see the brush write each one.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 這四個是我們照著摹本描的。點「在模型中看」，看毛筆怎麼寫出每一個。

zhi20.eyebrow: From the Scroll · 卷子裡的字
zhi20.lead_en: Here are all twenty, cut from a real copy of the scroll, in the order they appear. No. 13 is written heavily over other characters: even a famous work has corrections.
zhi20.lead_zh: 這是摹本裡全部二十個「之」，照出現的順序排。第 13 個寫得又黑又重，蓋在別的字上面——有名的作品也有塗改的地方。
zhi20.credit_html: Details of the Shenlong copy of the Lanting Xu. Wikimedia Commons (public domain). The scroll is in the Palace Museum, Beijing. · 維基共享資源（公有領域）；原卷藏北京故宮博物院。

same.lead_en: Look at the 之 in the big square, then find the one that is exactly the same among the four below. Look closely: they are all a little different.
same.lead_zh: 看看大格子裡的「之」，再從下面四個裡面，找出一模一樣的那一個。仔細看：每一個都有一點不一樣。

pad.lead_en: Choose one of the four forms and trace it. Each has a dot and one long zigzag line. The numbers tell you which 之 it is in the text.
pad.lead_zh: 從四個「之」裡選一個描寫看看。每個都是一點，加上一條彎來彎去的長線。數字是它在全文裡排第幾個。

tips.en: Write the dot first, then the zigzag line without lifting.
tips.zh: 先寫上面那一點，再一筆寫完彎彎的長線，中間不要提筆。

tips.en: Slow down at each turn, and speed up on the long lines.
tips.zh: 轉彎的地方慢一點，長線的地方快一點。

tips.en: After tracing all four, write a fifth one of your own.
tips.zh: 四個都描過以後，寫一個你自己的第五個「之」。

links_head.en: The scripts before, the essay itself, and what comes next
links_head.zh: 之前的字體、文章本身，和下一課

links.en: Regular, Running, Cursive: How Fast Can You Write?
links.zh: 楷書、行書、草書：同一個字，三種速度
links.note_en: The Lanting Xu is in running script: quicker than regular script, and still easy to read.
links.note_zh: 〈蘭亭序〉是行書：比楷書快，也還很容易認。

links.en: Preface to the Orchid Pavilion Collection
links.zh: 蘭亭集序
links.note_en: Read the whole essay with a line-by-line translation: a happy gathering, and then thoughts about time, life, and death.
links.note_zh: 讀全文與逐句白話翻譯：前半寫一場愉快的聚會，後半想到時間、生與死。

links.en: Strong Muscle, Hard Bone: Why Does Every Calligrapher's Writing Look Different?
links.zh: 顏筋柳骨：為什麼每個書法家的字都不一樣？
links.note_en: Tang dynasty masters learned from Wang Xizhi and then found styles of their own.
links.note_zh: 唐代的書法家向王羲之學習，再寫出自己的風格。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories of Wang Xizhi · 王羲之的故事
culture_cards.title_en: A scroll for a flock of geese, fans that sold out, a famous son-in-law, and a letter in Taipei
culture_cards.title_zh: 一卷字換一群鵝、賣光的扇子、東床快婿，和台北的一封短信
culture_cards.lead_en: Stories people have told about him for more than a thousand years, and one letter you can see in Taiwan. They are old stories; nobody can check every detail.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 一千多年來人們一直說著他的故事，還有一封在台灣看得到的短信。這些是古書裡的故事，細節沒有人能一一查證。

cards.en: A scroll for a flock of geese
cards.body_en: The history of the Jin dynasty says a Daoist priest in Shanyin kept fine geese. Wang Xizhi loved them and asked to buy them. The priest said: write out the Daodejing for me, and the whole flock is yours. Wang Xizhi gladly wrote it and carried the geese home in a cage, very pleased.
cards.body_zh: 《晉書》記載：山陰有一位道士養了好鵝，王羲之很喜歡，想跟他買。道士說：「為寫《道德經》，當舉群相贈耳。」王羲之欣然寫完，「籠鵝而歸，甚以為樂」。

cards.body_en: The same history tells of an old woman selling six-sided bamboo fans. Wang Xizhi wrote five characters on each one. She was upset at first. He told her: just say these were written by Wang Youjun, and ask a hundred coins. She did, and people rushed to buy them.
cards.body_zh: 《晉書》又說：王羲之看見一位老婆婆在賣六角竹扇，就在每把扇子上寫了五個字。老婆婆起先不高興，他說：「但言是王右軍書，以求百錢邪。」老婆婆照著說，大家搶著買。

cards.en: The young man on the east bed
cards.body_en: A Tales of the World story: a great official sent a messenger to the Wang family to choose a husband for his daughter. All the young men tried to look their best, except one, who lay on the east bed with his belly bare as if he had heard nothing. “That is the one!” said the official. It was Wang Xizhi. Today 東床 still means a son-in-law.
cards.body_zh: 《世說新語》的故事：太尉郗鑒派人到王家挑女婿。王家的年輕人個個裝得很端正，只有一個人「在東床上坦腹臥，如不聞」。郗鑒說：「正此好！」那個人就是王羲之。直到今天，「東床」還是女婿的意思。

cards.en: A letter about snow, in Taipei
cards.zh: 台北故宮的〈快雪時晴帖〉
cards.body_en: The National Palace Museum in Taipei keeps a short letter of Wang Xizhi's, Timely Clearing After Snowfall: four lines, 28 characters, beginning “Xizhi bows his head. After the quick snow, the sky has cleared.” The museum says it is a fine tracing copy made in the Tang dynasty. The Qianlong Emperor loved it and counted it among his Three Rarities. It is a National Treasure.
cards.body_zh: 台北國立故宮博物院藏有王羲之的一封短信〈快雪時晴帖〉：行書四行、二十八個字，開頭是「羲之頓首。快雪時晴，佳想安善」。故宮說它是唐代的精摹本。乾隆皇帝非常珍愛，把它列為「三希」之一。它是國寶。

myths.myth_en: Museums show the Lanting Xu that Wang Xizhi wrote himself.
myths.myth_zh: 博物館裡展出的〈蘭亭序〉是王羲之親筆寫的。
myths.fact_en: The original is lost. What museums have are copies made by hand in the Tang dynasty and later, and rubbings from stone carvings.
myths.fact_zh: 原蹟已經失傳。博物館裡的是唐朝和後來的人摹寫的本子，以及從刻石拓下來的拓本。

myths.myth_en: A great calligrapher writes the same character the same way every time.
myths.myth_zh: 厲害的書法家，同一個字每次都寫得一模一樣。
myths.fact_en: In the Lanting Xu it is the opposite. He Yanzhi wrote that every repeated character has a different form, and that the twenty or so 之 are all different.
myths.fact_zh: 〈蘭亭序〉正好相反。何延之說「有重者皆構別體」，二十來個「之」「變轉悉異，遂無同者」。

myths.myth_en: The Lanting Xu is only about a party.
myths.myth_zh: 〈蘭亭序〉只是在寫一場聚會。
myths.fact_en: It begins with the gathering, but then it turns to time, life, and death. You can read the whole essay in our Classical Chinese Prose series.
myths.fact_zh: 文章從聚會寫起，後半卻轉到時間、生與死。全文可以到我們的「古文選讀」讀。

myths.myth_en: Wang Xizhi invented running script.
myths.myth_zh: 行書是王羲之發明的。
myths.fact_en: Running script was already in use before him. He is remembered because he wrote it so well that later generations took his writing as their model.
myths.fact_zh: 在他以前就有行書了。大家記得他，是因為他寫得太好，後人都拿他的字當範本。

tricks.body_en: Third day of the third month, beside a winding stream.
tricks.body_zh: 三月三日，彎彎的小溪邊。

tricks.body_en: The cup floats; a guest drinks and chants.
tricks.body_zh: 酒杯漂過來，喝一杯、吟一首。

tricks.body_en: No two are alike.
tricks.body_zh: 變轉悉異，遂無同者。

tricks.body_en: We know it from copies.
tricks.body_zh: 今天看到的都是摹本和拓本。

safety.en: Ink stains clothes and is very hard to wash out. Wear old clothes or an apron, and roll up your sleeves.
safety.zh: 墨沾到衣服很難洗掉：穿舊衣服或圍裙，袖子捲起來。

safety.en: Cover the desk with old newspaper, and keep the ink in a heavy, steady dish so it will not tip over.
safety.zh: 桌上先鋪舊報紙；墨要裝在重一點、放得穩的碟子裡，免得打翻。

safety.en: Press gently. Crushing the brush against the paper squashes the hairs and can split or break them.
safety.zh: 輕輕地按就好：把筆用力壓在紙上，筆毛會擠扁，也可能分岔或折斷。

safety.en: Do not put the brush, the ink, or the ink stick in your mouth, and do not lick the brush tip to shape it.
safety.zh: 毛筆、墨汁、墨條都不要放進嘴裡，也不要用嘴巴舔筆尖。

safety.en: After writing, wash the brush in clean water until the water runs clear, gently shape it into a point, and hang it tip-down or lay it flat to dry. Wash your hands, too.
safety.zh: 寫完後用清水洗筆，洗到水變清為止；輕輕把筆毛理成尖形，筆尖朝下掛起來或平放晾乾。也要洗手。

activities.title_en: A Winding Stream in the Classroom

materials.en: Desks moved into a long winding line, with students sitting on both sides
materials.zh: 把桌子排成一條彎彎的長線，同學坐在兩邊

materials.en: A paper cup with a word card inside (no water needed)
materials.zh: 一個紙杯，裡面放一張字卡（不用裝水）

materials.en: Music, or a student who claps a beat
materials.zh: 音樂，或一位同學打拍子

steps.en: Pass the cup along the “stream” while the music plays.
steps.zh: 音樂響的時候，把紙杯沿著「小溪」一個傳一個。

steps.en: When the music stops, the student holding the cup takes out the card and reads the word.
steps.zh: 音樂一停，拿到紙杯的同學抽出字卡、唸出上面的字。

steps.en: That student says one line of a poem, or one English sentence, using the word.
steps.zh: 這位同學用那個字說一句詩，或造一個英文句子。

steps.en: Put in a new card and start the music again.
steps.zh: 換一張新的字卡，音樂再開始。

activities.tip_en: Use this lesson's vocabulary for the cards: stream, float, poem, gathering.
activities.tip_zh: 字卡可以用這一課的生字：stream、float、poem、gathering。

materials.en: A brush and water (or a pencil) and paper for each student
materials.zh: 每人一枝毛筆和清水（或鉛筆）、一張紙

materials.en: This lesson's picture of the twenty 之
materials.zh: 這一課「二十個之」的圖

steps.en: Choose three 之 from the picture and copy them as closely as you can.
steps.zh: 從圖裡選三個「之」，盡量照樣子臨寫。

steps.en: Now write two more of your own that are different from all three.
steps.zh: 再寫兩個你自己的「之」，要和前面三個都不一樣。

steps.en: Show your five to a partner. Which parts did you change: the dot, the turn, or the last line?
steps.zh: 把五個「之」給同伴看：你改了哪裡？那一點、轉彎，還是最後一筆？

steps.en: Pick the one you like best and say why.
steps.zh: 選出你最喜歡的一個，說說為什麼。

activities.tip_en: There is no wrong answer here. The point is to see how much one simple character can change.
activities.tip_zh: 這裡沒有標準答案，重點是看見一個簡單的字可以有多少變化。

sources.en: Wang Xizhi: served as General of the Right Army, so he is called Wang Youjun; later generations called him the Sage of Calligraphy (the dictionary gives his dates as 321–379; other sources differ)
sources.zh: 王羲之：嘗為右軍將軍，世稱王右軍；後人稱為「書聖」（辭典作西元 321～379，生卒年另有他說）
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「王羲之」

sources.en: Lanting Xu: written on the third day of the third month, 353, at the Orchid Pavilion in Shanyin, Kuaiji
sources.zh: 蘭亭集序：永和九年（西元 353）三月三日，會於會稽山陰的蘭亭，眾人賦詩，羲之自為作序
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「蘭亭集序」

sources.en: Floating cups on a winding stream: on the third day of the third month, people sat beside a winding stream, set wine cups afloat upstream, and whoever a cup stopped beside took it and drank
sources.zh: 流觴曲水：參加者坐在曲折環繞的水流旁，在上游放酒杯，任它順水流下，停在何處，則由某人取酒杯而飲
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「流觴曲水」

sources.en: 修禊: an old custom of washing at the water's edge in the third month to drive away bad luck
sources.zh: 修禊：於陰曆三月上巳日，臨水洗濯，借以祓除不祥
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「修禊」

sources.en: Text of the Lanting Xu: “崇山峻嶺，茂林修竹…清流激湍…引以為流觴曲水，列坐其次…一觴一詠”; the geese story; the fan story; “right army general”
sources.zh: 《晉書．王羲之傳》：〈蘭亭序〉全文（崇山峻嶺、茂林修竹、流觴曲水、一觴一詠）；寫經換鵝；老姥竹扇；右軍將軍、會稽內史
sources.src: 維基文庫《晉書》卷八十

sources.en: He Yanzhi, Lanting Ji (Tang): 28 lines, 324 characters; repeated characters all have different forms; 之 appears most, about twenty times, none alike; Emperor Taizong and the monk Biancai
sources.zh: 何延之〈蘭亭記〉（唐）：「凡二十八行，三百二十四字，有重者皆構別體。就中『之』字最多，乃有二十許個，變轉悉異，遂無同者」；唐太宗從辯才取得〈蘭亭〉的故事
sources.src: 維基文庫《法書要錄》卷三

sources.en: Wu Pingyi (Tang): when Emperor Taizong died, the original went into his tomb
sources.zh: 武平一〈徐氏法書記〉（唐）：「及太宗晏駕，本入玄宮」
sources.src: 維基文庫《法書要錄》卷三

sources.en: Our count: the Lanting Xu text has 之 twenty times (counted in the text and in the Shenlong copy)
sources.zh: 自己數的：〈蘭亭序〉全文「之」共二十個（原文與神龍本影像各數一次）
sources.src: 維基文庫〈蘭亭集序〉

sources.en: The Lanting Xu has long been called the best running script under heaven
sources.zh: 〈蘭亭序〉素有「天下第一行書」之稱
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院〈蘭亭癖〉展覽說明

sources.en: The original Lanting Xu is lost
sources.zh: 〈蘭亭序〉原蹟雖已失傳
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院典藏資料檢索〈定武蘭亭真本 卷〉

sources.en: 東床快婿: the story of Wang Xizhi being chosen as a son-in-law
sources.zh: 東床快婿：晉時王羲之坦腹東床被人選做女婿的故事
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「東床快婿」

sources.en: Image of the Shenlong copy of the Lanting Xu (public domain): source of the twenty 之 and reference for our tracings
sources.zh: 神龍本〈蘭亭序〉影像（公有領域）：二十個「之」的圖片來源與描線的對位參考
sources.src: Wikimedia Commons〈神龍蘭亭序全.JPG〉

sources.en: The earliest record of the numbers: 26 people wrote poems; 15 could not and were each fined wine (Liu Xiaobiao's notes, early 6th century, quoting Wang Xizhi's Linhe Xu). Song dynasty lists count 42 people instead.
sources.zh: 最早的人數記載：「二十六人，賦詩如左…十五人，不能賦詩，罰酒各三斗」（《世說新語．企羨》劉孝標注引〈臨河敘〉）；宋代的名單則是四十二人
sources.src: 維基文庫《世說新語．企羨》

sources.en: The Orchid Pavilion: southwest of Shaoxing, Zhejiang
sources.zh: 蘭亭：位於浙江省紹興縣西南
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「蘭亭」

sources.en: The son-in-law story: “on the east bed with his belly bare, as if he had not heard”
sources.zh: 《世說新語．雅量》：「唯有一郎，在東床上坦腹臥，如不聞。」郗公云：「正此好！」
sources.src: 維基文庫《世說新語．雅量》

sources.en: Timely Clearing After Snowfall: running script, four lines, 28 characters; a fine Tang tracing copy; one of Qianlong's Three Rarities
sources.zh: 〈快雪時晴帖〉：「本幅為唐代精摹本，行書四行二十八字」；乾隆將此帖與〈中秋帖〉〈伯遠帖〉合稱「三希」
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院典藏資料檢索〈晉王羲之快雪時晴帖 冊〉

sources.en: Timely Clearing After Snowfall: designated a National Treasure on March 26, 2012
sources.zh: 王羲之快雪時晴帖：國寶（2012-03-26 指定）
sources.src: 文化部文化資產局國家文化資產網

sources.en: Eared cup (耳杯): an oval drinking cup with an ear on each side, usually lacquer or bronze, common from the Warring States to the Jin
sources.zh: 耳杯：古代飲酒器，橢圓形，兩側各有一耳，多為木胎漆器或青銅器，盛行於戰國至晉代之間
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「耳杯」

sources.en: Running script before Wang Xizhi: “at the beginning of the Wei, Zhong and Hu practiced running script” (Wei Heng, d. 291)
sources.zh: 王羲之以前已有行書：衛恆《四體書勢》「魏初有鍾、胡二家為行書法」
sources.src: 維基文庫《四體書勢》

lessons.title: Strong Muscle, Hard Bone: Why Does Every Calligrapher's Writing Look Different?
lessons.title_zh: 顏筋柳骨：為什麼每個書法家的字都不一樣？
lessons.blurb_en: Yan Zhenqing and Liu Gongquan both wrote regular script in the Tang dynasty, yet you can tell them apart at a glance. Watch two brushes write the same character side by side in 3D, compare their press-and-lift curves, guess who wrote each character on real stone rubbings, and find out whose lines yours are closer to.
lessons.blurb_zh: 顏真卿和柳公權都是唐朝人，寫的都是楷書，可是一眼就分得出來。在 3D 裡看兩枝毛筆並排寫同一個字、比一比提按曲線，到真的拓本上猜猜每個字是誰寫的，再看看你的線條比較像誰。
lessons.big_idea_en: Every calligrapher writes the same characters with the same strokes, but each one presses, lifts, and shapes them in a different way. Yan Zhenqing's lines are thick and full; Liu Gongquan's are lean and firm. Later writers summed it up in four characters: 顏筋柳骨, the muscle of Yan and the bone of Liu.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 每一位書法家寫的是同樣的字、同樣的筆畫，可是下筆的輕重、提按的方式、字的形狀，每個人都不一樣。顏真卿的線條又粗又飽滿，柳公權的線條又瘦又挺。後人用四個字來形容：「顏筋柳骨」。

lab.title_en: Two Brushes, One Character: Yan and Liu
lab.title_zh: 兩枝筆寫同一個字：顏真卿和柳公權
lab.how_en: Drag to turn, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Two brushes write the same character at the same time: Yan Zhenqing's way on the left, Liu Gongquan's way on the right. Choose a character, replay one stroke at a time, and compare the two press-and-lift curves.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以旋轉，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。兩枝毛筆同時寫同一個字：左邊是顏真卿的寫法，右邊是柳公權的寫法。可以換字、一筆一筆重播，再比一比兩條提按曲線。

legend.en: Gold curve: how hard Yan's brush presses
legend.zh: 金色曲線：顏真卿的筆按得多重

legend.en: Blue curve: how hard Liu's brush presses
legend.zh: 藍色曲線：柳公權的筆按得多重

legend.en: Red grid: the same 25-cm square on both sheets
legend.zh: 紅色格線：兩張紙上一樣大的 25 公分方格

lab.scale_en: A teaching model. Both characters are drawn at the same size so that the lines can be compared, and the brushes move by the same speed rules. The center lines are our own tracings over rubbings of the Duobao Pagoda Stele (Yan, 752) and the Xuanmi Pagoda Stele (Liu, 841); the thickness of each line is measured from those rubbings. The widths in the table are for a 25-cm square, and they count only the main part of each stroke. A stone carving and its rubbing are not exactly what the brush wrote, so the numbers are a guide, not a measurement of the original writing.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型。兩個字放大到同樣大，線條才能比較；兩枝筆照同一套速度規則移動。中心線是我們對著〈多寶塔碑〉（顏，752 年）和〈玄秘塔碑〉（柳，841 年）的拓本自己描的，每一點的粗細是從拓本上量出來的。表格裡的寬度是字寫在 25 公分方格裡的大小，只算每一筆中間的行筆。刻在石頭上再拓下來的字，和毛筆當初寫的不會完全一樣，所以這些數字只是參考，不是原蹟的測量值。
lab.credit_html: Model, stroke data, and the writing engine are drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect. The two forms of each character are our own tracings over public-domain rubbings: Yan Zhenqing, Duobao Pagoda Stele (Wikimedia Commons; Tokyo National Museum) and Liu Gongquan, Xuanmi Pagoda Stele (Wikimedia Commons). · 模型、筆畫資料與寫字引擎由人師教育協會自繪、自寫；每個字的兩種寫法，是對著公有領域的拓本自己描的：顏真卿〈多寶塔碑〉（維基共享資源；東京國立博物館藏）、柳公權〈玄秘塔碑〉（維基共享資源）。

paras: Ask two friends to write the character 大. They will use the same three strokes in the same order, but the two characters will not look the same. Calligraphers are like that too. Two of the most famous, Yan Zhenqing and Liu Gongquan, both lived in the Tang dynasty and both wrote regular script, yet people can tell their writing apart at a glance.

Yan Zhenqing was an official in the 700s. His lines are thick and full, and his characters look broad and steady. He was also known for his courage. When the general An Lushan rebelled, most cities in the north fell, but Yan had quietly repaired the walls of his city, Pingyuan, and stored food, so it was ready. In his seventies he was sent to speak with another rebel, who killed him because he would not give in.

Liu Gongquan was born about seventy years later. His lines are leaner, with sharp corners and a tight center, like a strong, thin frame. One day the emperor asked him how to use the brush well. Liu answered, “Using the brush depends on the heart. When the heart is upright, the brush is upright.” The emperor understood that Liu was really giving him advice about how to rule.

Almost two hundred years after Liu died, the Song dynasty writer Fan Zhongyan praised a friend's calligraphy with four characters: 顏筋柳骨, “the muscle of Yan and the bone of Liu.” The words stuck. Muscle stands for Yan's full, powerful lines; bone stands for Liu's hard, clean ones. Both are praise: the phrase means writing that is strong.

Where does the difference come from? Not from the characters, and not from the stroke order. It comes from how hard the brush presses, where it lifts, how each stroke begins and ends, and how the strokes are spaced. In our model, when both write the same character at the same size, Yan's lines are 1.2 to 1.5 times as thick as Liu's.

For more than a thousand years, students have learned regular script by copying masters such as these two, stroke by stroke. People often name four great masters of regular script together: Ouyang Xun, Yan Zhenqing, Liu Gongquan, and Zhao Mengfu. In this lesson, watch two brushes write side by side, guess who wrote each character, and then try both styles yourself.
paras_zh: 請兩位同學各寫一個「大」字。他們用的是同樣的三筆、同樣的筆順，可是寫出來的兩個字不會一樣。書法家也是這樣。顏真卿和柳公權是最有名的兩位：都是唐朝人，寫的都是楷書，可是大家一眼就能分出誰是誰。
顏真卿是西元八世紀的官員。他的線條又粗又飽滿，字看起來寬闊、穩重。他也以勇敢聞名：安祿山叛變的時候，北方的城池大多失守，只有他守的平原城，因為早就悄悄修好城牆、存好糧食，所以守得住。七十多歲時，他奉命去勸說另一個叛將，因為不肯屈服而被殺害。
柳公權比顏真卿晚出生大約七十年。他的線條比較瘦，轉角銳利，字的中心收得很緊，像一副又瘦又結實的骨架。有一次，皇帝問他怎樣才能把筆用好，他回答：「用筆在心，心正則筆正。」皇帝聽懂了——柳公權其實是在勸他好好治理國家。
柳公權去世後將近兩百年，宋朝的范仲淹用四個字稱讚朋友的書法：「顏筋柳骨」。這四個字就這樣流傳下來。「筋」說的是顏真卿飽滿有力的線條，「骨」說的是柳公權堅硬俐落的線條。兩個都是稱讚：意思是字寫得很有力。
差別是從哪裡來的？不是字不一樣，也不是筆順不一樣，而是毛筆按得多重、在哪裡提起來、每一筆怎麼開始和結束、筆畫之間怎麼安排。在我們的模型裡，兩個人把同一個字寫成同樣大的時候，顏真卿的線條是柳公權的 1.2 到 1.5 倍粗。
一千多年來，學楷書的人都是照著像他們這樣的名家，一筆一筆臨摹。大家常把四位楷書名家合在一起說：歐陽詢、顏真卿、柳公權、趙孟頫。這一課，看兩枝毛筆並排寫字，猜猜每個字是誰寫的，再自己兩種寫法都試試看。
questions: How are Yan Zhenqing's lines different from Liu Gongquan's?
What did Liu Gongquan tell the emperor about using the brush?
If the characters and the stroke order are the same, where does the difference between two calligraphers come from?
answers: Yan's lines are thick and full, and his characters look broad and steady. Liu's lines are leaner, with sharp corners and a tight center.
He said that using the brush depends on the heart: when the heart is upright, the brush is upright.
From how hard the brush presses, where it lifts, how each stroke begins and ends, and how the strokes are spaced.

parts.meta_en: Tang dynasty · model: Duobao Pagoda Stele, 752
parts.text_en: Thick, full lines. The right-falling stroke swells into a heavy foot. The dictionary describes his writing as powerful, grand, and dignified.
parts.text_zh: 線條又粗又飽滿，捺的末端有厚重的捺腳。教育部辭典形容他的字「筆力勁拔，雄渾莊重」。

parts.meta_en: Tang dynasty · model: Xuanmi Pagoda Stele, 841
parts.text_en: Leaner lines with sharp corners, and the strokes pull in tightly toward the center. The dictionary describes his writing as strong in bone and tight in structure.
parts.text_zh: 線條比較瘦，轉角銳利，筆畫往字的中心收緊。教育部辭典形容他的字「骨力遒健，結構緊密」。

lessons.parts_note_en: These two 大 are our own tracings over the rubbings. Tap Watch it in 3D to see each one written.
lessons.parts_note_zh: 這兩個「大」是我們對著拓本描的。點「在模型中看」，看毛筆怎麼寫出來。

pad.en: Write like Yan, write like Liu
pad.zh: 學顏真卿寫，學柳公權寫
pad.lead_en: Choose a model and a character, then trace it. With a mouse or a finger, slow means thick and fast means thin. The bar shows whose lines yours are closer to.
pad.lead_zh: 選一位書法家的範本和一個字，描寫看看。用滑鼠或手指時，寫得慢線就粗、寫得快線就細。下面的橫條會告訴你，你的線條粗細比較接近誰。

tips.en: For Yan: go slowly and let every line grow thick and full.
tips.zh: 學顏：慢慢寫，讓每一筆都又粗又飽滿。

tips.en: For Liu: move a little faster, keep the lines thin, and stop firmly at each corner.
tips.zh: 學柳：寫快一點，線條細細的，轉角的地方穩穩停一下。

tips.en: Write the same character both ways and look at them side by side.
tips.zh: 同一個字用兩種方法各寫一次，放在一起看。

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories and Treasures · 故事與國寶
culture_cards.title_en: Four characters of praise, advice for an emperor, a draft full of grief, and a name worth gold
culture_cards.title_zh: 四個字的稱讚、給皇帝的忠告、滿紙悲傷的草稿，和值千金的名字
culture_cards.lead_en: Where the phrase comes from, what the history books say about the two men, and one work by Yan Zhenqing that you can see in Taipei.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 「顏筋柳骨」是怎麼來的、史書怎麼記這兩個人，還有一件在台北看得到的顏真卿真跡。

cards.en: Who first said 顏筋柳骨?
cards.body_en: In 1043 the Song dynasty statesman Fan Zhongyan wrote a farewell to his dead friend Shi Manqing. One line says, “Manqing's brush: the muscle of Yan, the bone of Liu.” So the phrase began as praise for a third person whose writing had the strengths of both. Later it came to describe Yan and Liu themselves.
cards.body_zh: 宋仁宗慶曆三年（1043），范仲淹為過世的朋友石曼卿寫了一篇祭文，裡面說：「曼卿之筆，顏筋柳骨。」（蘇軾引用的寫法）所以這四個字一開始，是稱讚「第三個人」的字兼有兩家的長處；後來才用來形容顏真卿和柳公權本人。

cards.en: “When the heart is upright, the brush is upright”
cards.body_en: The Old Book of Tang says that Emperor Muzong once asked Liu Gongquan how to use the brush perfectly. Liu replied, “Using the brush depends on the heart; when the heart is upright, the brush is upright.” The emperor's face changed: he knew Liu was using the brush to give him advice.
cards.body_zh: 《舊唐書》記載：唐穆宗「嘗問公權筆何盡善，對曰：『用筆在心，心正則筆正。』上改容，知其筆諫也。」——皇帝的臉色變了，因為他知道柳公權是藉著談毛筆來勸他。

cards.en: A draft full of grief, in Taipei
cards.body_en: In 758 Yan Zhenqing wrote a draft to mourn his nephew Jiming, who was killed in the rebellion. He crossed out and changed words as he went: an old note on the scroll counts 234 characters plus 34 crossed out. The Yuan dynasty collector Xianyu Shu called it “the second-best running script under heaven.” It is in the National Palace Museum in Taipei and is a National Treasure.
cards.body_zh: 乾元元年（758），顏真卿為在戰亂中遇害的姪子季明寫了一篇祭文的草稿。他邊寫邊塗改：卷後的舊題記數過，一共 234 個字，另外塗掉 34 個字。元代的鮮于樞稱它「天下行書第二」。這件作品收藏在台北的國立故宮博物院，是國寶。

cards.body_en: The Old Book of Tang says that when a great family set up a memorial stone and the writing was not by Liu Gongquan, people thought the children had failed in their duty to their parents. Envoys from other lands even brought a separate sum of money, marked “for buying Liu's calligraphy.”
cards.body_zh: 《舊唐書》說：「當時公卿大臣家碑板，不得公權手筆者，人以為不孝。外夷入貢，皆別署貨貝，曰此購柳書。」——大官家裡立碑，如果不是柳公權寫的，別人會覺得子孫不孝；外國使者來進貢，還特別另外準備一筆錢，寫明是「買柳公權的字」用的。

myths.myth_en: Yan Zhenqing's writing was always thick and heavy.
myths.myth_zh: 顏真卿的字一直都又粗又重。
myths.fact_en: The Duobao Pagoda Stele, which our model follows, is his earliest surviving work, written when he was 44. The National Palace Museum notes that it is cleaner and leaner than the grand, heavy style of his middle and later years.
myths.fact_zh: 我們模型參考的〈多寶塔碑〉是他傳世最早的作品，寫的時候四十四歲。故宮說這件作品「風格清勁，與中晚期的偉岸沉雄略有不同」——他後來的字更粗、更厚重。

myths.myth_en: “Muscle” is praise and “bone” is a complaint that Liu's writing is too thin.
myths.myth_zh: 「筋」是稱讚，「骨」是嫌柳公權的字太瘦。
myths.fact_en: Both words are praise. The dictionary explains that the writing of Yan and Liu is strong and vigorous, and that is why people say 顏筋柳骨.
myths.fact_zh: 兩個字都是稱讚。教育部辭典解釋：「唐代顏真卿、柳公權的書法，筆力遒勁，故稱為『顏筋柳骨』。」

myths.myth_en: The history books say Liu Gongquan learned from Yan Zhenqing.
myths.myth_zh: 史書說柳公權是跟顏真卿學的。
myths.fact_en: The Old Book of Tang says only that he first studied Wang Xizhi and then looked widely at recent writers before forming his own style. It was the Song writer Su Shi who thought Liu's writing came out of Yan's.
myths.fact_zh: 《舊唐書》只說他「初學王書，遍閱近代筆法，體勢勁媚，自成一家」。說「柳少師書，本出於顏」的是宋朝的蘇軾——那是蘇軾的看法。

myths.myth_en: Good handwriting proves that someone is a good person.
myths.myth_zh: 字寫得好，就證明這個人是好人。
myths.fact_en: Old writers such as Su Shi liked to say that writing resembles the person, and Yan Zhenqing's life fits the idea well. But that is a way of looking at art, not a rule. Handwriting gets better with practice.
myths.fact_zh: 蘇軾這些古人喜歡說「凡書象其為人」，顏真卿的一生也很符合這個說法。不過那是欣賞書法的一種看法，不是定律。字是練出來的。

tricks.title_en: Muscle of Yan, bone of Liu
tricks.body_en: Yan: thick and full. Liu: lean and firm.
tricks.body_zh: 顏：粗而飽滿。柳：瘦而挺拔。

tricks.body_en: Liu Gongquan's answer to the emperor.
tricks.body_zh: 柳公權回答皇帝的話。

tricks.body_en: Style comes from pressing, lifting, and spacing.
tricks.body_zh: 風格來自提按和結構。

tricks.body_en: Four masters of regular script people often name together.
tricks.body_zh: 大家常合稱的四位楷書名家。

safety.en: Ink stains clothes and is very hard to wash out. Wear old clothes or an apron, and roll up your sleeves.
safety.zh: 墨沾到衣服很難洗掉：穿舊衣服或圍裙，袖子捲起來。

safety.en: Cover the desk with old newspaper, and keep the ink in a heavy, steady dish so it will not tip over.
safety.zh: 桌上先鋪舊報紙；墨要裝在重一點、放得穩的碟子裡，免得打翻。

safety.en: Press gently. Crushing the brush against the paper squashes the hairs and can split or break them.
safety.zh: 輕輕地按就好：把筆用力壓在紙上，筆毛會擠扁，也可能分岔或折斷。

safety.en: Do not put the brush, the ink, or the ink stick in your mouth, and do not lick the brush tip to shape it.
safety.zh: 毛筆、墨汁、墨條都不要放進嘴裡，也不要用嘴巴舔筆尖。

safety.en: After writing, wash the brush in clean water until the water runs clear, gently shape it into a point, and hang it tip-down or lay it flat to dry. Wash your hands, too.
safety.zh: 寫完後用清水洗筆，洗到水變清為止；輕輕把筆毛理成尖形，筆尖朝下掛起來或平放晾乾。也要洗手。

materials.en: A brush and clean water, with newspaper or a water-writing cloth
materials.zh: 毛筆和清水，舊報紙或水寫布

materials.en: This page's side-by-side model, on a screen
materials.zh: 這一頁的並排模型（用螢幕看）

steps.en: Watch the two brushes write 十 in the model.
steps.zh: 先看模型裡兩枝筆寫「十」。

steps.en: Write 十 the Yan way: press down more and move slowly.
steps.zh: 學顏真卿寫一個「十」：按重一點、慢慢寫。

steps.en: Write 十 the Liu way: press less, keep the line thin, and stop firmly at the ends.
steps.zh: 學柳公權寫一個「十」：按輕一點、線條細細的，收筆穩穩停住。

steps.en: Do the same with 人 and 大. Show a partner and ask which is which.
steps.zh: 「人」和「大」也各寫兩種。給同伴看，請他猜哪個是哪一種。

activities.tip_en: Use water first. When you can make the two look different, try it with ink.
activities.tip_zh: 先用清水練。兩種寫得出差別以後，再用墨寫。

materials.en: Small cards and pencils or pens
materials.zh: 小卡片和鉛筆或原子筆

materials.en: A box to collect the cards
materials.zh: 一個收卡片的盒子

steps.en: Everyone writes the same three characters, 大 人 十, on a card, with no name.
steps.zh: 每個人在卡片上寫同樣的三個字「大、人、十」，不要寫名字。

steps.en: Mix the cards. Each group takes five and guesses who wrote each one.
steps.zh: 把卡片混在一起。每組抽五張，猜猜各是誰寫的。

steps.en: Say what clue you used: thick or thin lines? Big or small? Leaning or straight?
steps.zh: 說出你用的線索：線條粗還是細？字大還是小？歪的還是正的？

steps.en: Talk about it: what makes each person's writing their own?
steps.zh: 討論：每個人的字，是哪些地方讓它有自己的樣子？

activities.tip_en: Describe the writing, not the writer: every style has its strengths.
activities.tip_zh: 只描述字，不評論人：每一種風格都有它的長處。

sources.en: 顏筋柳骨: the calligraphy of Yan Zhenqing and Liu Gongquan is strong and vigorous, hence the phrase
sources.zh: 顏筋柳骨：「唐代顏真卿、柳公權的書法，筆力遒勁，故稱為『顏筋柳骨』。」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「顏筋柳骨」

sources.en: Yan Zhenqing: governor of Pingyuan; resisted An Lushan; killed by Li Xilie; writing powerful, grand, and dignified (the dictionary gives 708–784; the National Palace Museum gives 709–785)
sources.zh: 顏真卿：「玄宗時為平原太守，安祿山反，倡義討賊…德宗時李希烈反，受命前往慰諭，為所縊殺…筆力勁拔，雄渾莊重，與柳公權並稱顏柳。」（辭典作西元 708～784；故宮作 709～785，生卒年各說不一）
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「顏真卿」

sources.en: Liu Gongquan (778–865): strong in bone, tight in structure; known together with Yan Zhenqing as “Yan and Liu”
sources.zh: 柳公權：「（西元778～865）字誠懸…工書法，骨力遒健，結構緊密，體勢勁媚，自成一家。與顏真卿齊名，並稱『顏柳』。」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「柳公權」

sources.en: Ouyang Xun (557–641) and Zhao Mengfu (1254–1322)
sources.zh: 歐陽詢（西元557～641）「書體遒勁刻厲，自成一家」；趙孟頫（西元1254～1322）「工於書法，尤善行楷」

sources.en: Fan Zhongyan's farewell to Shi Manqing (1043), as quoted by Su Shi: “Manqing's brush: the muscle of Yan, the bone of Liu”
sources.zh: 蘇軾〈書石曼卿詩筆後〉引范仲淹祭文：「曼卿之筆，顏筋柳骨。散落人間，寶為神物。」（祭文作於慶曆三年；《宣和書譜》轉引作「延年之筆」）

sources.en: Fan Zhongyan's original text, dated the third year of Qingli (1043)

sources.src: 維基文庫《范文正公集》卷十

sources.en: “Using the brush depends on the heart”; memorial stones not written by Liu; envoys' money “for buying Liu's calligraphy”; he first studied Wang Xizhi
sources.zh: 「用筆在心，心正則筆正。」上改容，知其筆諫也；「當時公卿大臣家碑板，不得公權手筆者，人以為不孝。外夷入貢，皆別署貨貝，曰此購柳書」；「公權初學王書，遍閱近代筆法，體勢勁媚，自成一家」

sources.en: Yan Zhenqing at Pingyuan: he repaired the walls and stored food before An Lushan rebelled; his death at the hands of Li Xilie, aged 77
sources.zh: 「真卿以霖雨為托，修城浚池，陰料丁壯，儲廩實…祿山果反，河朔盡陷，獨平原城守具備」；「遂縊殺之，年七十七」
sources.src: 維基文庫《舊唐書》卷一百二十八

sources.en: The nephew Jiming was killed when his father refused to surrender
sources.zh: 「取少子季明加刃頸上曰：『降我，當活而子。』杲卿不答。遂並盧逖殺之。」
sources.src: 維基文庫《新唐書》卷一百九十二

sources.en: Draft of a Requiem to My Nephew: written in 758; 234 characters plus 34 crossed out; Xianyu Shu: “the second-best running script under heaven”
sources.zh: 〈祭姪文稿〉：「作於乾元元年（758）…文稿雖見增刪塗改，卻筆筆真情流露」；題跋「共計字二百三十四字。又塗抹三十四」；鮮于樞跋「天下行書第二。余家法書第一」

sources.src: 文化部文化資產局國家文化資產網

sources.zh: 〈多寶塔碑〉：「此碑是他傳世最早的作品，魯公書此碑時年四十四，因此風格清勁，與中晚期的偉岸沉雄略有不同。」

sources.zh: 〈多寶塔碑〉：「琅邪顏真卿書」「天寶十一載歲次壬辰四月…建」
sources.src: 維基文庫〈西京千福寺多寶佛塔感應碑〉

sources.zh: 〈玄秘塔碑〉：「裴休撰」「柳公權書并篆額」「會昌元年十二月廿八日建」

sources.zh: 蘇軾：「柳少師書，本出於顏，而能自出新意」；「凡書象其為人」

pairs.eyebrow: On the Stone · 碑帖上的字
pairs.lead_en: Each row is one character written by four masters of regular script. Look across a row: which is the thickest? Which has the sharpest corners? Three are rubbings from stone (white on black); Zhao Mengfu's is ink on paper.
pairs.lead_zh: 每一列是同一個字，由四位楷書名家寫的。橫著看一列：誰最粗？誰的轉角最銳利？前三位是從石碑拓下來的（黑底白字），趙孟頫的是寫在紙上的墨跡。
pairs.credit_html: Ouyang Xun, Jiucheng Palace inscription, reproduction of a Tang rubbing, National Diet Library, Japan (Wikimedia Commons, public domain); Yan Zhenqing, Duobao Pagoda Stele, Northern Song rubbing, Tokyo National Museum (Wikimedia Commons, public domain); Liu Gongquan, Xuanmi Pagoda Stele rubbing (Wikimedia Commons, public domain); Zhao Mengfu, Danba Stele handscroll, Palace Museum, Beijing (Wikimedia Commons, public domain). · 歐陽詢〈九成宮醴泉銘〉唐拓本複製本，日本國立國會圖書館藏；顏真卿〈多寶塔碑〉北宋拓本，東京國立博物館藏；柳公權〈玄秘塔碑〉拓本；趙孟頫〈帝師膽巴碑〉卷，北京故宮博物院藏（皆取自維基共享資源，公有領域）。

who.lead_en: Each character is cut from a real rubbing: the Duobao Pagoda Stele by Yan Zhenqing, or the Xuanmi Pagoda Stele by Liu Gongquan. We made the backgrounds the same, so you have to look at the lines.
who.lead_zh: 每個字都是從真的拓本上剪下來的：顏真卿的〈多寶塔碑〉，或柳公權的〈玄秘塔碑〉。我們把底色處理成一樣，所以要看線條才分得出來。

yan.hint_en: Yan's lines are thick and full, with heavy ends.
yan.hint_zh: 顏真卿的線條又粗又飽滿，收筆很厚重。

liu.hint_en: Liu's lines are leaner, with sharp corners and a tight center.
liu.hint_zh: 柳公權的線條比較瘦，轉角銳利，中心收得很緊。

who.credit_html: Rubbings: Yan Zhenqing, Duobao Pagoda Stele, Northern Song rubbing in the Tokyo National Museum (Wikimedia Commons, public domain); Liu Gongquan, Xuanmi Pagoda Stele (Wikimedia Commons, public domain). · 拓本：顏真卿〈多寶塔碑〉北宋拓本，東京國立博物館藏（維基共享資源，公有領域）；柳公權〈玄秘塔碑〉拓本（維基共享資源，公有領域）。 Backgrounds evened out by us; the shapes of the characters are unchanged. · 底色經過我們處理，字的形狀沒有改。

lessons.title: What Treasures of Calligraphy Can You See in Taiwan?
lessons.blurb_en: A letter about snow, a draft full of grief, a monk's wild cursive, a book about writing, and two poems from exile: five National Treasures of calligraphy are kept in Taipei. Walk through a 3D gallery, find out why the lights are so low, match details to the works, and look back over all ten lessons.
lessons.blurb_zh: 一封談雪的短信、一篇滿紙悲傷的草稿、一位和尚的狂草、一卷談寫字的書、兩首貶謫中寫的詩——五件書法國寶就收藏在台北。走進 3D 展廳，看看燈光為什麼這麼暗，用局部圖配對作品，再回顧這十堂課。
lessons.big_idea_en: Some of the most famous works of Chinese calligraphy are kept in the National Palace Museum in Taipei, and many are National Treasures. Paper and silk are harmed by light, and the harm adds up, so the museum keeps the lights low, shows each work for only a short time, and then lets it rest.
lessons.big_idea_zh: 許多最有名的書法作品收藏在台北的國立故宮博物院，其中不少是國寶。紙和絹怕光，而且光造成的傷害會累積，所以博物館把燈光調暗、每件作品只展出很短的時間，展完還要讓它休息。

lab.title_en: A Gallery of Five Treasures, and Why the Lights Are Low
lab.title_zh: 五件國寶的展廳，和燈光為什麼這麼暗
lab.how_en: Drag to look around, and scroll or pinch to zoom. Tap a work to walk up to it and read who wrote it, when, and in which script. Then choose Light: turn the light up, show a test strip for a year, and see why museums keep these rooms dim.
lab.how_zh: 拖曳可以環顧四周，滾輪或雙指可以縮放。點一件作品走近看：誰寫的、什麼時候、用哪一種字體。再選「燈光」：把燈調亮，讓一條試紙展出一年，看看博物館為什麼把展廳的燈開得這麼暗。

modes.text_en: The case holds a strip of dyed paper, half covered by a card. Choose a light level and put it on show. The museum's rule for its most protected works is no more than 16,000 lux-hours of light in a year.
modes.text_zh: 展櫃裡有一條染了顏色的試紙，一半用卡紙蓋住。選一種亮度，讓它展出。故宮對最需要保護的書畫的規定是：一年累積照到的光，不高於 16,000 lux・小時。

works.size_zh: 高 23 公分、寬 14.8 公分
works.text_en: A short letter of four lines and 28 characters, sending greetings after a snowfall. The museum says it is a fine tracing copy made in the Tang dynasty. The Qianlong Emperor called it “matchless under heaven.”
works.text_zh: 一封四行、二十八個字的短信，寫大雪初晴時對朋友的問候。故宮說它是唐代的精摹本。乾隆皇帝稱讚它「天下無雙，古今鮮對」。

works.text_en: A nine-meter scroll about how to write well, itself written in cursive script: 351 lines and about 3,700 characters. It is a book about calligraphy and a model of calligraphy at the same time.
works.text_zh: 一卷九公尺長、談「怎樣把字寫好」的文章，本身就用草書寫成：現存 351 行、約 3,700 多字。它既是書法理論，也是學草書的範本。

works.en: Draft of a Requiem to My Nephew
works.size_zh: 高 28.2 公分、長 77 公分
works.text_en: A draft written in grief for a nephew killed in the rebellion. The ink goes from wet to dry and many words are crossed out. The museum says these marks show the thoughts churning in the writer's mind.
works.text_zh: 為在戰亂中遇害的姪子寫的祭文草稿。墨色有濃有淡、有乾有濕，還有許多塗改。故宮說這些痕跡「顯露魯公振筆疾書時翻騰的思緒」。

works.size_zh: 高 28.3 公分、長 755 公分
works.text_en: The monk Huaisu tells how he learned to write, and copies out poems that friends wrote in praise of his cursive. The museum compares his round, turning lines to coiled steel cable.
works.text_zh: 和尚懷素寫自己學書法的經過，並抄下朋友們稱讚他草書的詩句。故宮形容他的筆畫「圓轉遒逸，如曲折盤繞的鋼索」。

works.size_en: 34.2 × 199.5 cm, with the note after it
works.size_zh: 高 34.2 公分、長 199.5 公分（含後面的題跋）
works.text_en: Two poems Su Shi wrote in exile in Huangzhou, on his third Cold Food Festival there. The characters start small and grow larger and heavier as the poems go on. His friend Huang Tingjian wrote beside it that even Su Shi might not write it so well a second time.
works.text_zh: 蘇軾被貶到黃州，在那裡過第三個寒食節時寫的兩首詩。字一開始比較小，越寫越大、越寫越重。朋友黃庭堅在後面題字說：就算叫東坡再寫一次，也未必寫得這麼好。

legend.en: Warm spotlights: one for each work
legend.zh: 暖色的投射燈：每件作品一盞

legend.en: Yellow label: the half of the strip in the light
legend.zh: 黃色標籤：試紙照到光的那一半

legend.en: Dark card: the half that stays covered
legend.zh: 深色卡紙：一直蓋住的那一半

lab.scale_en: A teaching model, not the real galleries: the room is our own simple design and the works are not to scale (all five are less than 35 cm tall). For the three long scrolls, the wall shows only the opening part or the main part. The light numbers are real: the museum's rules give 50 lux as the limit for paintings and calligraphy, and 16,000 lux-hours a year for its most protected works (for example, 50 lux for 8 hours a day for 40 days). The fading of the test strip is only an illustration of how light adds up; it is not a measurement of any real work, and the works on the wall never fade in the model.
lab.scale_zh: 這是教學用的示意模型，不是真的展廳：房間是我們自己設計的，作品也不是照比例（五件的高度都不到 35 公分）。三件長卷在牆上只放了開頭或主要的一段。燈光的數字是真的：故宮的規定是書畫照度不高於 50 lux，限展書畫一年累積不高於 16,000 lux・小時（例如 50 lux、每天 8 小時，可展 40 天）。試紙褪色的快慢只是用來說明「光會累積」的示意，不是任何一件文物的實測；牆上的作品在模型裡不會褪色。
lab.credit_html: Gallery model drawn and programmed by My Culture Connect. Works on the wall: 晉王羲之快雪時晴帖 冊。國立故宮博物院，台北，CC BY 4.0 @ www.npm.gov.tw（經裁切） 唐孫過庭書譜 卷。國立故宮博物院，台北，CC BY 4.0 @ www.npm.gov.tw（經裁切、拼接） 唐顏真卿祭姪文稿 卷。國立故宮博物院，台北，CC BY 4.0 @ www.npm.gov.tw（經裁切、拼接） 唐懷素自敘帖 卷。國立故宮博物院，台北，CC BY 4.0 @ www.npm.gov.tw（經裁切、拼接） 北宋蘇東坡書黃州寒食詩 卷。國立故宮博物院，台北，CC BY 4.0 @ www.npm.gov.tw（經裁切、拼接）

paras: Where can you see the real writing of the masters in this series? One answer is Taipei. The National Palace Museum there keeps more than 3,700 works of calligraphy, and some of them are among the most famous in the world.

The museum began in 1925 in the old palace in Beijing. In 1933, as war came closer, more than thirteen thousand crates of its treasures were sent south for safety. In 1948 and 1949, a selection of the finest pieces was shipped to Taiwan, and in 1965 a new museum building opened in Taipei.

This lesson looks at five works. Two were written by people you have already met: a short letter by Wang Xizhi, kept as a fine Tang dynasty copy, and Yan Zhenqing's draft for his nephew. Two are in cursive script: Sun Guoting's long scroll about how to write, and the wild cursive of the monk Huaisu. The last is by the Song dynasty poet Su Shi.

In 1080 Su Shi was sent away from the capital to live in Huangzhou. During his third Cold Food Festival there, in 1082, it rained and rained, and he wrote two sad poems. On the scroll, the characters begin small and grow larger and heavier as his feelings rise. The lower edge of the scroll is marked by fire. It was once taken to Japan, and the museum bought it in 1987.

You cannot see these works every day. Paper and silk are fragile, and light harms them a little at a time. The harm adds up and cannot be undone. So the museum keeps paintings and calligraphy at no more than 50 lux, which is far dimmer than daylight. Its most protected works may be shown for no more than 42 days, and then they rest for at least three years.

All five are National Treasures. After ten lessons, you can read them in a new way: you know the scripts, the strokes, and how a brush makes thick and thin lines. If you visit, walk slowly, look closely, and never use a flash.
paras_zh: 這個系列裡的書法家，他們真正寫的字要到哪裡看？其中一個答案是台北。台北的國立故宮博物院收藏了三千七百多件書法作品，有些是全世界最有名的。
故宮博物院 1925 年在北京的紫禁城成立。1933 年戰火逼近，一萬多箱文物被運到南方避難。1948、1949 年，其中挑選出來的精品用船運到台灣；1965 年，台北的新館落成開放。
這一課看五件作品。其中兩件的作者你已經認識：王羲之的一封短信（留下來的是唐代的精摹本），和顏真卿為姪子寫的草稿。兩件是草書：孫過庭談「怎麼寫字」的長卷，和和尚懷素的狂草。最後一件是宋朝詩人蘇軾寫的。
元豐三年（1080），蘇軾被貶離京城，到黃州居住。元豐五年（1082）他在那裡過第三個寒食節，雨下個不停，他寫了兩首悲傷的詩。在這卷字上，字一開始比較小，隨著情緒越來越激動，越寫越大、越寫越重。卷子的下緣有火燒過的痕跡。它曾經流落到日本，1987 年由故宮買回。
這些作品不是天天看得到。紙和絹很脆弱，光會一點一點地傷害它們；傷害會累積，而且無法復原。所以故宮規定書畫的照度不高於 50 lux——比白天的日光暗得多。最需要保護的那些「限展」書畫，一次最多展出 42 天，展完至少要休息三年。
這五件都是國寶。上完十堂課，你可以用新的眼光來看它們：你認得字體、認得筆畫，也知道毛筆怎麼寫出粗細。如果去參觀，請慢慢走、仔細看，而且絕對不要開閃光燈。

pad.lead_en: Three of the five treasures are in running script and two are in cursive. Trace 永, 之, and 水 once more in all three scripts, and time yourself. These models are from Lesson 7.
pad.lead_zh: 五件國寶裡有三件是行書、兩件是草書。再用三種字體描一次「永、之、水」，順便計時。這些範字是第七課的。

tips.en: Start with running script, the script of three of the five works.
tips.zh: 先寫行書——五件作品裡有三件是行書。

tips.en: Then try cursive: fewer lifts, and the strokes melt into each other.
tips.zh: 再試草書：提筆更少，筆畫融在一起。

tips.en: Go back to regular script last. Does it feel different now?
tips.zh: 最後回到楷書。現在寫起來，感覺有沒有不一樣？

culture_cards.eyebrow: Stories and a Visit · 故事與參觀
culture_cards.title_en: A scroll that survived fire, ten thousand banana plants, an emperor's favorite, and how to visit
culture_cards.title_zh: 逃過火災的卷子、一萬多株芭蕉、皇帝的最愛，和參觀須知
culture_cards.lead_en: Three stories that are written on the scrolls themselves or in old books, and what to know before you go.
culture_cards.lead_zh: 三個寫在卷子上或古書裡的故事，還有出發前要知道的事。

cards.body_en: Later owners wrote the scroll's story on the scroll itself. One note says it was marked by fire when the Summer Palace was burned in 1860. It later went to Japan, where its owner carried it out of the fires after the great Tokyo earthquake of 1923. After the Second World War it was bought back, and in 1987 the museum bought it.
cards.body_zh: 後來的收藏者把這卷字的遭遇寫在卷子後面。一則題跋說，1860 年圓明園被焚時它留下了燒痕。後來它流落到日本；1923 年關東大地震引起大火，收藏者冒險把它搶救出來。第二次世界大戰後它被買回，1987 年由故宮收購。

cards.body_en: A Tang dynasty life of Huaisu says he was too poor to buy paper, so he planted more than ten thousand banana plants at home to write on. When that was not enough, he wrote on a lacquered tray and a lacquered board, over and over, until he wore them through.
cards.body_zh: 唐朝陸羽寫的〈僧懷素傳〉說：懷素「貧無紙可書，嘗於故里種芭蕉萬餘株，以供揮灑。書不足，乃漆一盤書之，又漆一方板，書至再三，盤板皆穿。」——沒有紙，就種芭蕉來寫；還不夠，就寫在漆盤和漆板上，寫到都磨穿了。

cards.body_en: The Qianlong Emperor treasured Wang Xizhi's snow letter. The museum notes that he praised it as “matchless under heaven, rarely equaled in any age,” and kept it with two other works as his “Three Rarities.” You can still see his writing and seals all around the four lines.
cards.body_zh: 乾隆皇帝非常珍愛〈快雪時晴帖〉。故宮說他「譽之為『天下無雙，古今鮮對』」，並把它和另外兩件作品合稱「三希」。直到今天，那四行字的周圍還看得到他題的字和蓋的印章。

cards.body_en: The museum is at No. 221, Section 2, Zhishan Road, Shilin District, Taipei. These works are not always on show, so check the museum's website first. Flash, extra lights, tripods, and selfie sticks are not allowed. The galleries are kept at 20 to 24 degrees Celsius, so bring a jacket.
cards.body_zh: 故宮在臺北市士林區至善路二段 221 號。這些作品不是隨時都在展出，出發前先上故宮的網站查。展場拍照「禁止使用閃光燈、補光器材、腳架、自拍器」。展廳溫度維持在攝氏 20 到 24 度，記得帶件外套。

myths.myth_en: The museum's most famous works are always on show.
myths.myth_zh: 故宮最有名的作品隨時都看得到。
myths.fact_en: Most paintings and calligraphy are shown for no more than three months and then rest for at least eighteen months. The seventy most protected works are shown for no more than 42 days at a time.
myths.fact_zh: 一般書畫「展出期間以不超過三個月為原則，每次展出後須歸庫養護至少十八個月」；七十件限展書畫精華，一次最多展 42 天。

myths.myth_en: Timely Clearing After Snowfall is in Wang Xizhi's own hand.
myths.myth_zh: 〈快雪時晴帖〉是王羲之親筆寫的。
myths.fact_en: The museum describes it as a fine tracing copy made in the Tang dynasty. As Lesson 8 told, the original of his Lanting Xu is lost too.
myths.fact_zh: 故宮的說明是「本幅為唐代精摹本」。第八課說過，他的〈蘭亭序〉原蹟也已經失傳。

myths.myth_en: Ancient critics ranked the Cold Food scroll “the third-best running script under heaven.”
myths.myth_zh: 古人把〈寒食帖〉評為「天下第三行書」。
myths.fact_en: We could not find any old source for that ranking. What the records do have is the Ming dynasty artist Dong Qichang, who called it the best of Su Shi's writing. Grouping it with the Lanting Xu and Yan Zhenqing's draft as the three great works of running script is a later habit.
myths.fact_zh: 這個排名找不到古人的出處。有記錄的是明朝董其昌稱它為「蘇書甲觀」。把它和〈蘭亭序〉、〈祭姪文稿〉合稱三大行書，是後人的說法。

myths.myth_en: The lights are low because black ink fades quickly.
myths.myth_zh: 燈光暗，是因為黑色的墨很容易褪色。
myths.fact_en: Carbon ink is one of the materials least harmed by light. What light harms more are the paper, the silk, and their colors. That is why our test strip in the model uses dyes, not ink.
myths.fact_zh: 碳做的墨是最不怕光的材料之一。比較怕光的是紙、絹和上面的顏色。所以模型裡的試紙用的是染料，不是墨。

tricks.body_en: Snow letter, treatise, draft, autobiography, Cold Food.
tricks.body_zh: 快雪、書譜、祭姪、自敘、寒食。

tricks.body_en: Light × time: the harm cannot be undone.
tricks.body_zh: 照度 × 時間：傷害無法復原。

tricks.body_en: 50 lux; 42 days; three years of rest.
tricks.body_zh: 50 lux；42 天；休息三年。

tricks.body_en: Walk slowly and look closely.
tricks.body_zh: 慢慢走，仔細看。

safety.en: Ink stains clothes and is very hard to wash out. Wear old clothes or an apron, and roll up your sleeves.
safety.zh: 墨沾到衣服很難洗掉：穿舊衣服或圍裙，袖子捲起來。

safety.en: Cover the desk with old newspaper, and keep the ink in a heavy, steady dish so it will not tip over.
safety.zh: 桌上先鋪舊報紙；墨要裝在重一點、放得穩的碟子裡，免得打翻。

safety.en: Press gently. Crushing the brush against the paper squashes the hairs and can split or break them.
safety.zh: 輕輕地按就好：把筆用力壓在紙上，筆毛會擠扁，也可能分岔或折斷。

safety.en: Do not put the brush, the ink, or the ink stick in your mouth, and do not lick the brush tip to shape it.
safety.zh: 毛筆、墨汁、墨條都不要放進嘴裡，也不要用嘴巴舔筆尖。

safety.en: After writing, wash the brush in clean water until the water runs clear, gently shape it into a point, and hang it tip-down or lay it flat to dry. Wash your hands, too.
safety.zh: 寫完後用清水洗筆，洗到水變清為止；輕輕把筆毛理成尖形，筆尖朝下掛起來或平放晾乾。也要洗手。

materials.en: Two sheets of colored construction paper (the same color)
materials.zh: 兩張同樣顏色的色紙

materials.en: A piece of thick card and some tape
materials.zh: 一塊厚紙板和膠帶

materials.en: A sunny windowsill and a drawer
materials.zh: 曬得到太陽的窗台，和一個抽屜

steps.en: Tape the card over half of one sheet and put it on the sunny windowsill.
steps.zh: 用厚紙板蓋住其中一張色紙的一半，放在窗台上曬太陽。

steps.en: Put the other sheet in a dark drawer.
steps.zh: 另一張放進黑暗的抽屜。

steps.en: After two weeks, take off the card and compare the three: sunlit, covered, and drawer.
steps.zh: 兩個星期後拿掉紙板，比較三個地方：曬到太陽的、被蓋住的、抽屜裡的。

steps.en: Talk about it: which museum rules does this explain?
steps.zh: 討論：這個實驗可以解釋博物館的哪些規定？

activities.tip_en: Take a photo on the first day so you can compare.
activities.tip_zh: 第一天先拍一張照片，之後才好比較。

materials.en: This page's five works, on a screen or printed
materials.zh: 這一頁的五件作品（用螢幕看或印出來）

materials.en: Cards and pens for labels
materials.zh: 寫說明牌的卡片和筆

steps.en: Each group chooses one of the five works.
steps.zh: 每組從五件作品裡選一件。

steps.en: Write a museum label in English: who, when, which script, and one sentence about why it is special.
steps.zh: 用英文寫一張說明牌：誰寫的、什麼時候、哪一種字體，再用一句話說它特別的地方。

steps.en: Decide how long your work may be on show, and how you will protect it from light.
steps.zh: 決定你的作品可以展多久，以及要怎麼保護它不被光傷害。

steps.en: Hold a five-work exhibition and give a one-minute tour.
steps.zh: 辦一場五件作品的小展覽，每組導覽一分鐘。

activities.tip_en: Good labels are short. Try to use fewer than forty words.
activities.tip_zh: 好的說明牌很短。試試看不超過四十個英文字。

sources.en: Museum history: founded October 10, 1925; treasures moved south in 1933 (13,427 crates and 64 bundles); shipped to Taiwan in 1948–49; the new Taipei building opened on November 12, 1965
sources.zh: 院史：「1925年10月10日，故宮博物院正式成立」；1933 年「故宮文物共13,427箱又64包，計分五批啟運」；1948 年秋「主張擇精品運臺」；1965 年「11月12日，國立故宮博物院臺北新館落成揭幕」
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院〈院史〉

sources.en: Collection: 3,757 works of calligraphy (as of September 30, 2026)
sources.zh: 典藏統計：「法書－3,757件」（截至 115 年 9 月 30 日）
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院〈典藏概述〉

sources.en: Light limits: paintings and calligraphy no more than 50 lux; restricted works no more than 16,000 lux-hours a year (for example, 50 lux, 8 hours a day, 40 days); UV below 75 microwatts per lumen
sources.zh: 「書畫、紙、絹…不高於50 Lux」「限展書畫之年累積照度不高於16,000Lux．h/year為原則」「例如50Lux，每天8小時，可展40天」「紫外線強度低於七十五微瓦/流明」
sources.src: 〈國立故宮博物院文物展覽保存維護要點〉

sources.en: Most paintings and calligraphy: shown for no more than three months, then at least eighteen months in storage
sources.zh: 「展出期間以不超過三個月為原則，每次展出後須歸庫養護至少十八個月。」
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院主管法規共用系統

sources.en: The seventy restricted works: no more than 42 days on show
sources.zh: 「若屬『七十件限展書畫精華』，展期則以42天為上限。」
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院展覽說明

sources.en: At least three years between showings, and no more than 42 days
sources.zh: 「為了加強保護珍貴古物，減少被光線照射的時間，每次展覽至少必須間隔三年以上，而且展期不能超過 42 天。」
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院展覽說明

sources.en: Light dose is light level times time; 50 lux is the museum benchmark; carbon ink is among the least light-sensitive materials
sources.zh: 累積曝光量＝照度 × 時間；50 lux 是博物館的基準；碳墨屬於最不怕光的材料
sources.src: Canadian Conservation Institute, “Agent of Deterioration: Light, Ultraviolet and Infrared”

sources.en: Draft of a Requiem to My Nephew: museum record (故書000060)
sources.zh: 〈唐顏真卿祭姪文稿 卷〉典藏頁（故書000060）：作者、書體、年代、尺寸與說明

sources.zh: 〈唐懷素自敘帖 卷〉典藏頁（故書000062）：作者、書體、年代、尺寸與說明

sources.zh: 〈北宋蘇東坡書黃州寒食詩 卷〉典藏頁（購書001001）：作者、書體、年代、尺寸與說明
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院典藏資料檢索

sources.en: All five were designated National Treasures on March 26, 2012 (this link: the Cold Food scroll, with its history: about 1949 to a Taipei collector; bought by the museum in 1987)
sources.zh: 五件都在 2012-03-26 指定為國寶（此連結：寒食帖，含流傳經過「約一九四九年歸台北收藏家，一九八七年故宮購回」與「蘇書甲觀」）
sources.src: 文化部文化資產局國家文化資產網

sources.en: Su Shi: sent to Huangzhou; built a house on the Eastern Slope and called himself Dongpo
sources.zh: 「以黃州團練副使安置。軾與田父野老，相從溪山間，築室於東坡，自號『東坡居士』。」
sources.src: 維基文庫《宋史》卷三百三十八

sources.en: Cold Food Festival: one or two days before Qingming, when no fires were lit
sources.zh: 寒食節：「每年冬至後一百零五日，約在清明節前一、二日」「禁火寒食」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「寒食節」

sources.en: Huaisu planted more than ten thousand banana plants to write on
sources.zh: 「貧無紙可書，嘗於故里種芭蕉萬餘株，以供揮灑。」
sources.src: 維基文庫 陸羽〈僧懷素傳〉

sources.en: Wild cursive: flourished in the Tang dynasty with Zhang Xu and Huaisu
sources.zh: 狂草：「至唐代張旭、懷素時盛行。狂草筆勢縱逸不拘，連綿迴繞」
sources.src: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》「狂草」

sources.en: Visiting rules: no flash, extra lights, tripods, or selfie sticks; galleries kept at 20–24°C
sources.zh: 「展場拍照或攝影禁止使用閃光燈、補光器材、腳架、自拍器等輔助設備」「展廳溫度維持在攝氏20度至24度間」
sources.src: 國立故宮博物院〈展場參觀須知〉

sources.en: Taiwan curriculum: know stories of famous calligraphers (4-Ⅱ-8); appreciate famous works (4-Ⅳ-4)
sources.zh: 十二年國教國語文領綱：4-Ⅱ-8「知道古今書法名家的故事。」4-Ⅳ-4「認識各種書體，欣賞名家碑帖。」
sources.src: 國家教育研究院《十二年國民基本教育課程綱要 語文領域—國語文》

sheets.en: Look closely: a detail from each
sheets.zh: 靠近一點看：每一件的局部
sheets.lead_en: These are real details from the five works, from the museum's open data. Before you read the caption, ask yourself: which script is it? Is the ink wet or dry? Do the characters stay the same size?
sheets.lead_zh: 這是五件作品真的局部，來自故宮的開放資料。先別看說明，問問自己：這是哪一種字體？墨是濕的還是乾的？字的大小一樣嗎？

tline.en: Seven hundred years on one line
tline.lead_en: From Wang Xizhi's time to Su Shi's is about seven hundred years. Three of the five works were written within ninety years of each other in the Tang dynasty.
tline.lead_zh: 從王羲之到蘇軾，大約七百年。五件裡有三件是唐朝寫的，前後相差不到九十年。

items.note_zh: 王羲之的信；留下來的是唐代的精摹本。

match.lead_en: Here is a small piece of one of the five works. Which one is it from? Use what you know about scripts, ink, and the size of the characters.

kuaixue.hint_en: Four short lines of calm running script, with many red seals around them.
kuaixue.hint_zh: 四行從容的行書，周圍蓋了很多紅色的印章。

shupu.hint_en: Small, quick cursive in neat columns: each character stands alone.
shupu.hint_zh: 小小的、寫得很快的草書，一行一行很整齊，字和字多半不相連。

jizhi.hint_en: A draft: look for dry, scratchy ink and words crossed out.
jizhi.hint_zh: 這是草稿：找找乾乾的枯筆，和塗掉的字。

zixu.hint_en: Wild cursive: thin, round lines that loop on and on, with some characters suddenly huge.
zixu.hint_zh: 狂草：細細圓圓的線一直繞下去，有些字突然寫得很大。

recap.en: Look how far you have come
recap.lead_en: This is the last lesson in the series. Here are all ten, with one sentence each. Tap any lesson to go back.
recap.lead_zh: 這是這個系列的最後一課。十堂課各用一句話回顧，點任何一課都可以回去看。

items.en: Brush, ink, paper, and inkstone: the four tools of writing.
items.zh: 筆、墨、紙、硯：寫字的四樣工具。

items.en: Press for thick, lift for thin.
items.zh: 按下去就粗，提起來就細。

items.en: The character 永 holds eight basic strokes.
items.zh: 一個「永」字，藏著八種基本筆法。

items.en: Stroke order gives everyone the same path through a character.
items.zh: 筆順讓每個人用同一條路線寫一個字。

items.en: Characters began as pictures on bones and bronze.
items.zh: 文字從甲骨和青銅器上的圖畫開始。

items.en: Clerical script flattened the curves and added the swallow tail.
items.zh: 隸書把彎的拉直，還多了一個燕尾。

items.en: Regular, running, and cursive: one character, three speeds.
items.zh: 楷、行、草：同一個字，三種速度。

items.en: Wang Xizhi wrote 之 twenty times, and no two are alike.
items.zh: 王羲之寫了二十個「之」，沒有兩個一樣。

items.en: Yan's muscle and Liu's bone: same strokes, different pressure.
items.zh: 顏筋柳骨：筆畫一樣，輕重不同。

items.en: The treasures are in Taipei, resting in dim light.
items.zh: 國寶就在台北，在暗暗的燈光下休息。
